verses.text_gb: 神和[Fn1]主耶稣基督的[Cra]奴仆[Fn2]雅各，写信给[Fn3][Crb]散居的[Fn4]十二个[Crc]支派：[Fn5]愿你们喜乐。
verses.text_big5: 神和[Fn1]主耶穌基督的[Cra]奴僕[Fn2]雅各，寫信給[Fn3][Crb]散居的[Fn4]十二個[Crc]支派：[Fn5]願你們喜樂。
verses.text_en: James, a slave of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes in the dispersion: Rejoice!
verses.text_gb_plain: 神和主耶稣基督的奴仆雅各，写信给散居的十二个支派：愿你们喜乐。
verses.text_big5_plain: 神和主耶穌基督的奴僕雅各，寫信給散居的十二個支派：願你們喜樂。

footnotes.zh: 雅各将主耶稣与神列为同等，这与不承认主神格的犹太教(约五18)相反。
footnotes.zh_big5: 雅各將主耶穌與神列為同等，這與不承認主神格的猶太教（約五18）相反。
footnotes.en: 1:1 1 James A flesh brother of the Lord Jesus (Matt. 13:55) and of Jude (Jude 1:1). He was not one of the twelve apostles chosen by the Lord while He was on earth, but he became an apostle after the Lord's resurrection (Gal. 1:19), and he became the leading elder in the church at Jerusalem (Acts 12:17; 15:2, 13; 21:18). Reputed to be, with Peter and John, a pillar of the church, he was mentioned by Paul as the first among the three pillars (Gal. 2:9).

footnotes.zh: 雅各是主耶稣(太十三55)和犹大(犹1)肉身的兄弟。他不是主在地上时所拣选的十二使徒之一，但在主复活后成了一位使徒(加一19)，并且是在耶路撒冷的召会中领头的长老(徒十二17，十五2，13，二一18)；他与彼得、约翰同被称为召会的柱石，且被保罗提为三柱石之首(加二9)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 雅各是主耶穌（太十三55）和猶大（猶1）肉身的兄弟。他不是主在地上時所揀選的十二使徒之一，但在主復活後成了一位使徒，（加一19，）並且是在耶路撒冷的召會中領頭的長老；（徒十二17，十五2，13，二一18；）他與彼得、約翰同被稱為召會的柱石，且被保羅題為三柱石之首。（加二9。）
footnotes.en: 1:1 2 Lord James ranked the Lord Jesus as equal with God. This was contrary to Judaism, which did not recognize the deity of the Lord (John 5:18).

footnotes.zh: 见彼前一1注3。这该包括那些在五旬节后，因逼迫从耶路撒冷分散出去的犹太信徒(徒八1，4)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 見彼前一1註3。這該包括那些在五旬節後，因逼迫從耶路撒冷分散出去的猶太信徒。（徒八1，4。）
footnotes.en: 1:1 3 twelve The tribes of Israel. This indicates that this Epistle was written to the Jewish Christians, who had the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ of glory (James 2:1) and were justified by faith (James 2:24), regenerated by the word of truth (v. 18), and indwelt by the Spirit of God (James 4:5), and who were members of the church (James 5:14), awaiting the Lord's coming back (James 5:7-8). However, for the writer to call these believers in Christ "the twelve tribes," as God's chosen people were called in His Old Testament economy, might indicate that he lacked a clear view concerning the distinction between Christians and Jews, between God's New Testament economy and the Old Testament dispensation. Perhaps he did not see that in the New Testament God had delivered and separated the Jewish believers in Christ from the Jewish people, who were then considered by God a perverse generation (Acts 2:40). In His New Testament economy, God does not consider the Jewish believers to be Jews set apart for Judaism but Christians set apart for the church. As members of the church of God, they should be as distinct and separate from the Jews as they are from the Gentiles (1 Cor. 10:32). Yet James, a pillar of the church, in his Epistle to the Christian brothers still called them "the twelve tribes." (This might have been the reason that he addressed the word in James 5:1-6 to the rich class in general among the Jews.) This was contrary to God's New Testament economy. See note James 2:2 1 .

footnotes.zh: 指以色列的众支派。这指明本书信是写给犹太的基督徒，他们相信我们荣耀的主耶稣基督(二1)，本于信得称义(二24)，因真理的话得了重生(18)，为神的灵所内住(四5)；他们也是召会的肢体(五14)，等候主的回来(五7～8)。然而，称这些在基督里的信徒为十二个支派，如同神旧约经纶里的选民，也可能指明作者对基督徒与犹太人，神新约经纶与旧约安排的分别，以及神在新约里已经将在基督里的犹太信徒，从神所看为弯曲世代(徒二40)的犹太人中拯救、圣别出来，缺少清楚的看见。神在祂新约的经纶里，看犹太信徒不再是为着犹太教的犹太人，乃是为着召会的基督徒。他们是神的召会，应当与犹太人不同，从犹太人中分别出来，就像他们应当与外邦人不同，从外邦人中分别出来一样(林前十32)。然而，作召会柱石的雅各，在他写给基督徒弟兄的书信里，仍然称他们为十二个支派(这也许是他向犹太人中间一般富有的阶层，说了五1～6那段话的原因)。这违反了神新约的经纶。见二2注1。
footnotes.zh_big5: 指以色列的眾支派。這指明本書信是寫給猶太的基督徒，他們相信我們榮耀的主耶穌基督，（二1，）本於信得稱義，（二24，）因真理的話得了重生，（18，）為神的靈所內住；（四5；）他們也是召會的肢體，（五14，）等候主的回來。（五7～8。）然而，稱這些在基督裏的信徒為十二個支派，如同神舊約經綸裏的選民，指明作者對基督徒與猶太人，神新約經綸與舊約安排的分別，以及神在新約裏已經將在基督裏的猶太信徒，從神所看為彎曲世代（徒二40）的猶太人中拯救、聖別出來，缺少清楚的看見。神在祂新約的經綸裏，看猶太信徒不再是為著猶太教的猶太人，乃是為著召會的基督徒。他們是神的召會，應當與猶太人不同，從猶太人中分別出來，就像他們應當與外邦人不同，從外邦人中分別出來一樣。（林前十32。）然而，作召會柱石的雅各，在他寫給基督徒弟兄的書信裏，仍然稱他們為十二個支派。（這也許是他向猶太人中間一般富有的階層，說了五1～6那段話的原因。）這違反了神新約的經綸。見二2註1。
footnotes.en: 1:1 4 dispersion See note 1 Pet. 1:1 4 . This dispersion must have included the scattering of the Jewish believers from Jerusalem caused by the persecution after Pentecost (Acts 8:1, 4).

footnotes.zh: 见约贰10注3。
footnotes.zh_big5: 見約貳10註3。
footnotes.en: 1:1 5 Rejoice See note 2 John 1:10 3 .

refs.text_gb: 基督耶稣的奴仆保罗，蒙召的使徒，被分别出来归于神福音的；
refs.text_big5: 基督耶穌的奴僕保羅，蒙召的使徒，被分別出來歸於神福音的；
refs.text_en: Paul, a slave of Christ Jesus, a called apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,

refs.text_gb: 耶稣基督的奴仆和使徒西门彼得，写信给那些因我们的神和救主，耶稣基督的义，与我们分得同样宝贵之信的人：
refs.text_big5: 耶穌基督的奴僕和使徒西門彼得，寫信給那些因我們的神和救主，耶穌基督的義，與我們分得同樣寶貴之信的人：
refs.text_en: Simon Peter, a slave and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have been allotted faith equally precious as ours in the righteousness of our God and Savior, Jesus Christ:

refs.text_gb: 耶稣基督的奴仆，雅各的兄弟犹大，写信给那蒙召，在父神里蒙爱，并蒙耶稣基督保守的人：
refs.text_big5: 耶穌基督的奴僕，雅各的兄弟猶大，寫信給那蒙召，在父神裏蒙愛，並蒙耶穌基督保守的人：
refs.text_en: Jude, a slave of Jesus Christ and a brother of James, to those who are called, beloved in God the Father, and kept by Jesus Christ:

refs.text_gb: 我原想，我要将他们分散，我要使人间不再记念他们；
refs.text_big5: 我原想，我要將他們分散，我要使人間不再記念他們；
refs.text_en: I would have said, I will scatter them, / I will cause the memory of them to cease from among men;

refs.text_gb: 我在旷野也向他们举手起誓，必将他们分散在列国，四散在各地；
refs.text_big5: 我在曠野也向他們舉手起誓，必將他們分散在列國，四散在各地；
refs.text_en: I also lifted up My hand to them in the wilderness that I would scatter them among the nations and would disperse them among the countries,

refs.text_gb: 犹太人就彼此说，这人要往哪里去，叫我们找不着？难道祂要往散居在希利尼人中的犹太人那里，去教训希利尼人么？
refs.text_big5: 猶太人就彼此說，這人要往那裏去，叫我們找不著？難道祂要往散居在希利尼人中的猶太人那裏，去教訓希利尼人麼？
refs.text_en: The Jews then said to one another, Where is this man about to go that we will not find Him? Is He about to go to the Jews in dispersion among the Greeks and teach the Greeks?

refs.text_gb: 这应许，我们十二个支派昼夜切切地事奉神，都盼望得着；王啊，我被犹太人控告，就是因这盼望。
refs.text_big5: 這應許，我們十二個支派晝夜切切的事奉神，都盼望得著；王阿，我被猶太人控告，就是因這盼望。
refs.text_en: To which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, O king.

refs.text_gb: 叫你们在我国里，坐在我的席上吃喝，并且坐在宝座上，审判以色列十二个支派。
refs.text_big5: 叫你們在我國裏，坐在我的席上喫喝，並且坐在寶座上，審判以色列十二個支派。
refs.text_en: That you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom; and you will sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

verses.text_gb: 我的[Cra]弟兄们，无论何时你们落在诸般的[Fn1][Crb]试炼中，都要以为大[Crc]喜乐；
verses.text_big5: 我的[Cra]弟兄們，無論何時你們落在諸般的[Fn1][Crb]試煉中，都要以為大[Crc]喜樂；
verses.text_en: Count it all joy, my brothers, whenever you fall into various trials,
verses.text_gb_plain: 我的弟兄们，无论何时你们落在诸般的试炼中，都要以为大喜乐；
verses.text_big5_plain: 我的弟兄們，無論何時你們落在諸般的試煉中，都要以為大喜樂；

footnotes.en: 1:2 1 trials See note James 1:12 1 .

refs.text_gb: 我亲爱的弟兄们，不要看错了。
refs.text_big5: 我親愛的弟兄們，不要看錯了。
refs.text_en: Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.

refs.text_gb: 我亲爱的弟兄们，这是你们所知道的，但你们各人要快快地听，慢慢地说，慢慢地动怒；
refs.text_big5: 我親愛的弟兄們，這是你們所知道的，但你們各人要快快的聽，慢慢的說，慢慢的動怒；
refs.text_en: You know this, my beloved brothers; but let every man be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath;

refs.text_gb: 我的弟兄们，你们既相信我们荣耀的主耶稣基督，便不可按着外貌待人。
refs.text_big5: 我的弟兄們，你們既相信我們榮耀的主耶穌基督，便不可按著外貌待人。
refs.text_en: My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ of glory with respect of persons.

refs.text_gb: 我亲爱的弟兄们，请听，神岂不是拣选了世上贫穷的人，叫他们在信上富足，并承受祂所应许给那些爱祂之人的国么？
refs.text_big5: 我親愛的弟兄們，請聽，神豈不是揀選了世上貧窮的人，叫他們在信上富足，並承受祂所應許給那些愛祂之人的國麼？
refs.text_en: Listen, my beloved brothers: Did not God choose the poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom, which He promised to those who love Him?

refs.text_gb: 我的弟兄们，若有人说自己有信心，却没有行为，有什么益处？难道这信心能救他么？
refs.text_big5: 我的弟兄們，若有人說自己有信心，卻沒有行為，有甚麼益處？難道這信心能救他麼？
refs.text_en: What is the profit, my brothers, if anyone says he has faith but does not have works? Can that faith save him?

refs.text_gb: 我的弟兄们，不要多人作教师，因为知道我们要受更重的审判。
refs.text_big5: 我的弟兄們，不要多人作教師，因為知道我們要受更重的審判。
refs.text_en: Do not become many teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive greater judgment.

refs.text_gb: 颂赞和咒诅从同一个口里出来，我的弟兄们，这是不应当的。
refs.text_big5: 頌讚和咒詛從同一個口裏出來，我的弟兄們，這是不應當的。
refs.text_en: Out of the same mouth come forth blessing and cursing. These things, my brothers, ought not to be so.

refs.text_gb: 我的弟兄们，无花果树能生橄榄么？葡萄树能结无花果么？咸水也不能发出甜水来。
refs.text_big5: 我的弟兄們，無花果樹能生橄欖麼？葡萄樹能結無花果麼？鹹水也不能發出甜水來。
refs.text_en: Can a fig tree, my brothers, produce olives? Or a vine, figs? Neither can salt water produce sweet.

refs.text_gb: 弟兄们，你们不可彼此批评；那批评弟兄，或审判弟兄的，就是批评律法，审判律法。你若审判律法，就不是行律法者，乃是审判者。
refs.text_big5: 弟兄們，你們不可彼此批評；那批評弟兄，或審判弟兄的，就是批評律法，審判律法。你若審判律法，就不是行律法者，乃是審判者。
refs.text_en: Do not speak against one another, brothers. He who speaks against a brother or judges his brother speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.

refs.text_gb: 所以，弟兄们，你们要恒忍，直到主的来临。看哪，农夫等候地里宝贵的出产，为此恒忍，直到得了秋雨春雨。
refs.text_big5: 所以，弟兄們，你們要恆忍，直到主的來臨。看哪，農夫等候地裏寶貴的出產，為此恆忍，直到得了秋雨春雨。
refs.text_en: Therefore be long-suffering, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer eagerly awaits the precious fruit of the earth, exercising long-suffering over it until it receives the early and late rain.

refs.text_gb: 弟兄们，你们不要彼此埋怨，免得受审判；看哪，那审判者站在门前了。
refs.text_big5: 弟兄們，你們不要彼此埋怨，免得受審判；看哪，那審判者站在門前了。
refs.text_en: Do not complain, brothers, against one another lest you be judged. Behold, the Judge stands before the doors.

refs.text_gb: 弟兄们，你们要把那曾在主名里说话的众申言者，当作受苦和恒忍的榜样。
refs.text_big5: 弟兄們，你們要把那曾在主名裏說話的眾申言者，當作受苦和恆忍的榜樣。
refs.text_en: As an example, brothers, of suffering evil and of long-suffering, take the prophets, who spoke in the name of the Lord.

refs.text_gb: 我的弟兄们，最要紧的是不可起誓；不可指着天起誓，也不可指着地起誓，无论何誓都不可起；你们的话，是，就说是，不是，就说不是，免得你们落在审判之下。
refs.text_big5: 我的弟兄們，最要緊的是不可起誓；不可指著天起誓，也不可指著地起誓，無論何誓都不可起；你們的話，是，就說是，不是，就說不是，免得你們落在審判之下。
refs.text_en: But above all things, my brothers, do not swear, neither by heaven nor by earth nor with any other oath; but let your yes be yes, and your no, no, lest you fall under judgment.

refs.text_gb: 我的弟兄们，你们中间若有人受迷惑离开真理，有人使他回转，
refs.text_big5: 我的弟兄們，你們中間若有人受迷惑離開真理，有人使他回轉，
refs.text_en: My brothers, if any one among you is led astray from the truth and someone turns him back,

refs.text_gb: 忍受试炼的人有福了，因为他既受试验得了称许，就必得着生命的冠冕，这是主应许给那些爱祂之人的。
refs.text_big5: 忍受試煉的人有福了，因為他既受試驗得了稱許，就必得著生命的冠冕，這是主應許給那些愛祂之人的。
refs.text_en: Blessed is the man who endures trial, because when he has become approved by testing, he will receive the crown of life, which He promised to those who love Him.

refs.text_gb: 在那时期你们要欢腾，尽管目前在诸般的试炼中，或许必须暂时忧愁，
refs.text_big5: 在那時期你們要歡騰，儘管目前在諸般的試煉中，或許必須暫時憂愁，
refs.text_en: In which time you exult, though for a little while at present, if it must be, you have been made sorrowful by various trials,

refs.text_gb: 应当喜乐欢腾，因为你们在诸天之上的赏赐是大的；原来在你们以前的申言者，人也是这样逼迫他们。
refs.text_big5: 應當喜樂歡騰，因為你們在諸天之上的賞賜是大的；原來在你們以前的申言者，人也是這樣逼迫他們。
refs.text_en: Rejoice and exult, for your reward is great in the heavens; for so they persecuted the prophets who were before you.

refs.text_gb: 倒要照着你们有分于基督苦难的多少而欢乐，使你们在祂荣耀显现的时候，也可以喜乐欢腾。
refs.text_big5: 倒要照著你們有分於基督苦難的多少而歡樂，使你們在祂榮耀顯現的時候，也可以喜樂歡騰。
refs.text_en: But inasmuch as you share in the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, so that also at the revelation of His glory you may rejoice exultingly.

verses.text_gb: 知道你们[Fn1]信心所受的[Cra]试验，产生[Crb]忍耐。
verses.text_big5: 知道你們[Fn1]信心所受的[Cra]試驗，產生[Crb]忍耐。
verses.text_en: Knowing that the proving of your faith works out endurance.
verses.text_gb_plain: 知道你们信心所受的试验，产生忍耐。
verses.text_big5_plain: 知道你們信心所受的試驗，產生忍耐。

footnotes.zh: 指神在基督里所赐基督徒的信心(彼后一1，雅二1)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 指神在基督裏所賜基督徒的信心。（彼後一1，雅二1。）
footnotes.en: 1:3 1 faith The Christian faith, given by God in Christ (2 Pet. 1:1; James 2:1).

refs.text_gb: 忍受试炼的人有福了，因为他既受试验得了称许，就必得着生命的冠冕，这是主应许给那些爱祂之人的。
refs.text_big5: 忍受試煉的人有福了，因為他既受試驗得了稱許，就必得著生命的冠冕，這是主應許給那些愛祂之人的。
refs.text_en: Blessed is the man who endures trial, because when he has become approved by testing, he will receive the crown of life, which He promised to those who love Him.

refs.text_gb: 叫你们信心所受的试验，比那经过火的试验仍会毁坏之金子的试验，更为宝贵，可以在耶稣基督显现的时候，显为可得称赞、荣耀和尊贵的；
refs.text_big5: 叫你們信心所受的試驗，比那經過火的試驗仍會毀壞之金子的試驗，更為寶貴，可以在耶穌基督顯現的時候，顯為可得稱讚、榮耀和尊貴的；
refs.text_en: So that the proving of your faith, much more precious than of gold which perishes though it is proved by fire, may be found unto praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ;

refs.text_gb: 不但如此，就是在患难中，我们也是夸耀，因为知道患难生忍耐，
refs.text_big5: 不但如此，就是在患難中，我們也是誇耀，因為知道患難生忍耐，
refs.text_en: And not only so, but we also boast in our tribulations, knowing that tribulation produces endurance;

refs.text_gb: 在知识上供应节制，在节制上供应忍耐，在忍耐上供应敬虔，
refs.text_big5: 在知識上供應節制，在節制上供應忍耐，在忍耐上供應敬虔，
refs.text_en: And in knowledge, self-control; and in self-control, endurance; and in endurance, godliness;

verses.text_gb: 但[Cra]忍耐也当成功，好使你们[Fn1][Crb]齐备完整，毫无缺欠。
verses.text_big5: 但[Cra]忍耐也當成功，好使你們[Fn1][Crb]齊備完整，毫無缺欠。
verses.text_en: And let endurance have its perfect work that you may be perfect and entire, lacking in nothing.
verses.text_gb_plain: 但忍耐也当成功，好使你们齐备完整，毫无缺欠。
verses.text_big5_plain: 但忍耐也當成功，好使你們齊備完整，毫無缺欠。

footnotes.zh: 虽然雅各可能没有清楚看见恩典与律法的分别，但论到基督徒的品行，他的书信却是特殊且显著的强调基督徒实行的完全，说到信徒应当齐备完整，毫无缺欠。这可视为本书的主题。这种基督徒行为上的完全，需要神行政对付的试炼(2，12)，并信徒凭那借着栽种的话得蒙重生(18，21)之神圣出生的效能而有的忍耐。
footnotes.zh_big5: 雖然雅各沒有清楚看見恩典與律法的分別，但論到基督徒的品行，他的書信卻是特殊且顯著的強調基督徒實行的完全，說到信徒應當齊備完整，毫無缺欠。這可視為本書的主題。這種基督徒行為上的完全，需要神行政對付的試煉，（2，12，）並信徒憑那藉著栽種的話得蒙重生（18，21）之神聖出生的效能而有的忍耐。
footnotes.en: 1:4 1 perfect Although James might not have had a clear view concerning the distinction between grace and law, his Epistle is distinguished and remarkable in its presentation of Christian conduct, emphasizing practical Christian perfection that the believers might be perfect and entire, lacking in nothing. This may be considered the main subject of this Epistle. Such perfection in Christian behavior requires the trials of God's governmental dealing and the believers' endurance by the virtue of the divine birth through regeneration by the implanted word (vv. 18, 21).

refs.text_gb: 忍耐生老练，老练生盼望，
refs.text_big5: 忍耐生老練，老練生盼望，
refs.text_en: And endurance, approvedness; and approvedness, hope;

refs.text_gb: 我们在许多事上都有过失，若有人在话语上没有过失，他就是完全人，也能勒住全身。
refs.text_big5: 我們在許多事上都有過失，若有人在話語上沒有過失，他就是完全人，也能勒住全身。
refs.text_en: For in many things we all stumble. If anyone does not stumble in word, this one is a perfect man, able to bridle the whole body as well.

refs.text_gb: 所以你们要完全，像你们的天父完全一样。
refs.text_big5: 所以你們要完全，像你們的天父完全一樣。
refs.text_en: You therefore shall be perfect as your heavenly Father is perfect.

refs.text_gb: 且愿和平的神，亲自全然圣别你们，又愿你们的灵、与魂、与身子得蒙保守，在我们主耶稣基督来临的时候，得以完全，无可指摘。
refs.text_big5: 且願和平的神，親自全然聖別你們，又願你們的靈、與魂、與身子得蒙保守，在我們主耶穌基督來臨的時候，得以完全，無可指摘。
refs.text_en: And the God of peace Himself sanctify you wholly, and may your spirit and soul and body be preserved complete, without blame, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.text_gb: 你们中间若有缺少[Fn1][Cra]智慧的，就当[Fn2][Crb]求那[Fn3]厚赐众人，也[Fn4]不斥责人的神，就必有赐给他的。
verses.text_big5: 你們中間若有缺少[Fn1][Cra]智慧的，就當[Fn2][Crb]求那[Fn3]厚賜眾人，也[Fn4]不斥責人的神，就必有賜給他的。
verses.text_en: But if any one of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and does not reproach, and it will be given to him.
verses.text_gb_plain: 你们中间若有缺少智慧的，就当求那厚赐众人，也不斥责人的神，就必有赐给他的。
verses.text_big5_plain: 你們中間若有缺少智慧的，就當求那厚賜眾人，也不斥責人的神，就必有賜給他的。

footnotes.zh: 神乃是借着祂的智慧，在基督里定了祂永远的计划，并将其完成(林前二7，弗三9～11，箴八12，22～31)。并且神在祂新约的经纶里，先使基督成为我们的智慧(林前一24，30)。神的智慧是基督徒实行的完全所必需的，所以我们需要向神求智慧。 照本书信的内容看，雅各对神新约的经纶似乎没有清楚的看见，但他有智慧描述实行之基督徒生活的事。
footnotes.zh_big5: 神乃是藉著祂的智慧，在基督裏定了祂永遠的計畫，並將其完成。（林前二7，弗三9～11，箴八12，22～31。）並且神在祂新約的經綸裏，先使基督成為我們的智慧。（林前一24，30。）神的智慧是基督徒實行的完全所必需的，所以我們需要向神求智慧。ˍ照本書信的內容看，雅各對神新約的經綸顯然沒有清楚的看見，但他有智慧描述實行之基督徒生活的事。
footnotes.en: 1:5 1 wisdom It was by His wisdom that God, in Christ, made His eternal plan and carried it out (1 Cor. 2:7; Eph. 3:9-11; Prov. 8:12, 22-31). And in His New Testament economy God made Christ first our wisdom (1 Cor. 1:24, 30). The wisdom of God is needed for practical Christian perfection. Hence, we need to ask God for it. In light of the content of this Epistle, it seems that James did not have a clear vision concerning God's New Testament economy. However, he did have the wisdom to portray matters that concern the practical Christian life.

footnotes.zh: 雅各被称为祷告的人。他在这里嘱咐受信者要祷告求智慧，含示他的智慧是借着祷告蒙神所赐的。他在本书信里强调祷告(五14～18)。祷告乃是基督徒实行之完全的美德。
footnotes.zh_big5: 雅各被稱為禱告的人。他在這裏囑咐受信者要禱告求智慧，含示他的智慧是藉著禱告蒙神所賜的。他在本書信裏強調禱告。（五14～18。）禱告乃是基督徒實行之完全的美德。
footnotes.en: 1:5 2 ask James was reputed to be a man of prayer. Here he charged the recipients of his Epistle to pray for wisdom, implying that his wisdom was given to him by God through prayer. In his Epistle he stressed prayer (James 5:14-18). Prayer is a virtue of practical Christian perfection.

footnotes.zh: 厚，或，单纯的，慷慨的，毫无保留的(罗十二8，林后八2)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 厚，或，單純的，慷慨的，毫無保留的。（羅十二8，林後八2。）
footnotes.en: 1:5 3 liberally Or, with simplicity, generously, without reserve (Rom. 12:8; 2 Cor. 8:2).

footnotes.zh: 吝啬的人不肯给人；就是给，也会说些冷酷、刻薄的话。但那厚赐众人的神，不像这样的人。
footnotes.zh_big5: 吝嗇的人不肯給人；就是給，也會說些冷酷、刻薄的話。但那厚賜眾人的神，不像這樣的人。
footnotes.en: 1:5 4 not A stingy man would not give; if he were to give, he would give with reproaches, with stinging words. God, who gives to all liberally, is not like such a man.

refs.text_gb: 你们中间谁是有智慧有见识的？他就当用智慧的温柔，凭他美好的品行，显出他所作所为的。
refs.text_big5: 你們中間誰是有智慧有見識的？他就當用智慧的溫柔，憑他美好的品行，顯出他所作所為的。
refs.text_en: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his good manner of life his works in meekness of wisdom.

refs.text_gb: 唯独从上头来的智慧，先是纯洁的，后是和平的、和蔼的、柔顺的，满有怜悯和善果，没有偏见，没有假冒。
refs.text_big5: 惟獨從上頭來的智慧，先是純潔的，後是和平的、和藹的、柔順的，滿有憐憫和善果，沒有偏見，沒有假冒。
refs.text_en: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, forbearing, compliant, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, without hypocrisy.

refs.text_gb: 所以求你赐仆人聪明的心，可以审断你的民，能辨别善恶。不然，谁能审断你这众多的民呢？
refs.text_big5: 所以求你賜僕人聰明的心，可以審斷你的民，能辨別善惡。不然，誰能審斷你這眾多的民呢？
refs.text_en: Give therefore to Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people and to discern between good and evil. For who is able to judge this great people of Yours?

refs.text_gb: 所罗门求这事，他的话在主眼中看为美。
refs.text_big5: 所羅門求這事，他的話在主眼中看為美。
refs.text_en: And this word seemed good in the sight of the Lord, that Solomon had asked for this matter.

refs.text_gb: 神对他说，你既然求这事，不为自己求长寿、求财富，也不求灭绝你仇敌的性命，单为自己求辨识可以听讼，
refs.text_big5: 神對他說，你既然求這事，不為自己求長壽、求財富，也不求滅絕你仇敵的性命，單為自己求辨識可以聽訟，
refs.text_en: And God said to him, Because you have asked for this matter and have not asked for long life for yourself and have not asked for riches for yourself and have not asked for the life of your enemies, but have asked for discernment for yourself to understand justice;

refs.text_gb: 我就照你的话而行。看哪，我赐你智慧和明辨的心，甚至在你以前没有像你的，在你以后也没有兴起来像你的。
refs.text_big5: 我就照你的話而行。看哪，我賜你智慧和明辨的心，甚至在你以前沒有像你的，在你以後也沒有興起來像你的。
refs.text_en: I now do according to your words. I now give you a heart of wisdom and understanding, so that there has been no one like you before you, nor will one rise up after you like you.

refs.text_gb: 侧耳听智慧，倾心求聪明；
refs.text_big5: 側耳聽智慧，傾心求聰明；
refs.text_en: Making your ear attentive to wisdom / And inclining your heart to understanding;

refs.text_gb: 因为耶和华赐人智慧；知识和聪明都由祂口而出；
refs.text_big5: 因為耶和華賜人智慧；知識和聰明都由祂口而出；
refs.text_en: For Jehovah gives wisdom; / From His mouth come knowledge and understanding;

refs.text_gb: 坏人不明白公理，唯有寻求耶和华的，明白一切。
refs.text_big5: 壞人不明白公理，惟有尋求耶和華的，明白一切。
refs.text_en: Evil men do not understand justice, / But those who seek Jehovah understand all things.

refs.text_gb: 所以我告诉你们，凡你们祷告祈求的，无论是什么，只要信已经得着了，就必得着。
refs.text_big5: 所以我告訴你們，凡你們禱告祈求的，無論是甚麼，只要信已經得著了，就必得著。
refs.text_en: For this reason I say to you, All things that you pray and ask, believe that you have received them, and you will have them.

verses.text_gb: 只是要凭着[Cra]信心求，一点不[Fn1][Crb]疑惑；因为那疑惑的人，就像[Crc]海中的波浪，被[Crd]风吹动翻腾。
verses.text_big5: 只是要憑著[Cra]信心求，一點不[Fn1][Crb]疑惑；因為那疑惑的人，就像[Crc]海中的波浪，被[Crd]風吹動翻騰。
verses.text_en: But let him ask in faith, doubting nothing, for he who doubts is like the surge of the sea, driven by the wind and tossed about.
verses.text_gb_plain: 只是要凭着信心求，一点不疑惑；因为那疑惑的人，就像海中的波浪，被风吹动翻腾。
verses.text_big5_plain: 只是要憑著信心求，一點不疑惑；因為那疑惑的人，就像海中的波浪，被風吹動翻騰。

refs.text_gb: 所以我告诉你们，凡你们祷告祈求的，无论是什么，只要信已经得着了，就必得着。
refs.text_big5: 所以我告訴你們，凡你們禱告祈求的，無論是甚麼，只要信已經得著了，就必得著。
refs.text_en: For this reason I say to you, All things that you pray and ask, believe that you have received them, and you will have them.

refs.text_gb: 耶稣就摸他们的眼睛，说，照着你们的信，给你们成就了吧！
refs.text_big5: 耶穌就摸他們的眼睛，說，照著你們的信，給你們成就了罷！
refs.text_en: Then He touched their eyes, saying, According to your faith, let it be done to you.

refs.text_gb: 于是耶稣回答她说，妇人，你的信心真大！照你所愿的给你成全吧。从那时候，她的女儿就得了医治。
refs.text_big5: 於是耶穌回答她說，婦人，你的信心真大！照你所願的給你成全罷。從那時候，她的女兒就得了醫治。
refs.text_en: Then Jesus answered and said to her, O woman, great is your faith! Be it done to you as you wish. And her daughter was healed from that hour.

refs.text_gb: 人非有信，就不能得神的喜悦；因为到神面前来的人，必须信有神，且信祂赏赐那寻求祂的人。
refs.text_big5: 人非有信，就不能得神的喜悅；因為到神面前來的人，必須信有神，且信祂賞賜那尋求祂的人。
refs.text_en: But without faith it is impossible to be well pleasing to Him, for he who comes forward to God must believe that He is and that He is a rewarder of those who diligently seek Him.

refs.text_gb: 耶稣回答他们说，我实在告诉你们，你们若有信心，不疑惑，不但能行无花果树上所发生的事，就是对这座山说，你得挪开，投在海里，也必成就。
refs.text_big5: 耶穌回答他們說，我實在告訴你們，你們若有信心，不疑惑，不但能行無花果樹上所發生的事，就是對這座山說，你得挪開，投在海裏，也必成就。
refs.text_en: And Jesus answered and said to them, Truly I say to you, If you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, Be taken up and cast into the sea, it will happen.

refs.text_gb: 总没有因不信而疑惑神的应许，反倒因信得着加力，将荣耀归与神，
refs.text_big5: 總沒有因不信而疑惑神的應許，反倒因信得著加力，將榮耀歸與神，
refs.text_en: But with regard to the promise of God, he did not doubt in unbelief, but was empowered by faith, giving glory to God

refs.text_gb: 唯独恶人，好像翻腾的海，不得平静，其中的水，常涌出污秽和淤泥来。
refs.text_big5: 惟獨惡人，好像翻騰的海，不得平靜，其中的水，常湧出污穢和淤泥來。
refs.text_en: But the wicked are like the tossed sea, / For it cannot be calm, / And its waters toss up mire and mud.

refs.text_gb: 是海里的狂浪，涌出自己可耻的泡沫；是流荡的星，有黑暗的幽冥为他们永远存留。
refs.text_big5: 是海裏的狂浪，湧出自己可恥的泡沫；是流蕩的星，有黑暗的幽冥為他們永遠存留。
refs.text_en: Wild waves of the sea, foaming out their own shames; wandering stars, for whom the gloom of darkness is kept for eternity.

refs.text_gb: 使我们不再作小孩子，为波浪漂来漂去，并为一切教训之风所摇荡，这教训是在于人的欺骗手法，在于将人引入错谬系统的诡诈作为；
refs.text_big5: 使我們不再作小孩子，為波浪漂來漂去，並為一切教訓之風所搖蕩，這教訓是在於人的欺騙手法，在於將人引入錯謬系統的詭詐作為；
refs.text_en: That we may be no longer little children tossed by waves and carried about by every wind of teaching in the sleight of men, in craftiness with a view to a system of error,

refs.text_gb: 这样的人，在你们的爱筵上乃是暗礁，与你们同吃的时候，无所惧怕；他们是只喂养自己的牧人；是没有雨水的云彩，被风飘荡；是秋天没有果子的树，死而又死，连根被拔出来；
refs.text_big5: 這樣的人，在你們的愛筵上乃是暗礁，與你們同喫的時候，無所懼怕；他們是只餧養自己的牧人；是沒有雨水的雲彩，被風飄蕩；是秋天沒有果子的樹，死而又死，連根被拔出來；
refs.text_en: These are the hidden reefs in your love feasts, feasting together with you without fear, shepherding themselves; waterless clouds being carried off by winds; autumn trees without fruit, having died twice, rooted up;

verses.text_gb: 这样的人，不要想从主那里得到什么；
verses.text_big5: 這樣的人，不要想從主那裏得到甚麼；
verses.text_en: For that man must not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord;
verses.text_gb_plain: 这样的人，不要想从主那里得到什么；
verses.text_big5_plain: 這樣的人，不要想從主那裏得到甚麼；

verses.text_gb: [Fn1][Cra]心怀二意的人，在他一切的路上，都是摇荡不定的。
verses.text_big5: [Fn1][Cra]心懷二意的人，在他一切的路上，都是搖蕩不定的。
verses.text_en: He is a double-souled man, unstable in all his ways.
verses.text_gb_plain: 心怀二意的人，在他一切的路上，都是摇荡不定的。
verses.text_big5_plain: 心懷二意的人，在他一切的路上，都是搖蕩不定的。

footnotes.zh: 直译，双魂的人。神只给人造一个魂，具有一个心思、一个意志。信徒在祷告中疑惑，就使自己成了双魂的人，好像船有了双舵，方向不定。在祷告中的信心，也是基督徒实行之完全的美德。
footnotes.zh_big5: 直譯，雙魂的人。神只給人造一個魂，具有一個心思、一個意志。信徒在禱告中疑惑，就使自己成了雙魂的人，好像船有了雙舵，方向不定。在禱告中的信心，也是基督徒實行之完全的美德。
footnotes.en: 1:8 1 double God made man only one soul, with one mind and one will. When a believer doubts in prayer, he makes himself double-souled, like a boat with two rudders, uncertain in direction. Faith in prayer also is a virtue of practical Christian perfection.

refs.text_gb: 你们要亲近神，神就必亲近你们。有罪的人哪，要洁净你们的手。心怀二意的人哪，要纯洁你们的心。
refs.text_big5: 你們要親近神，神就必親近你們。有罪的人哪，要潔淨你們的手。心懷二意的人哪，要純潔你們的心。
refs.text_en: Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-souled!

verses.text_gb: 卑微的弟兄[Fn1][Cra]升高，就该[Fn2]夸耀；
verses.text_big5: 卑微的弟兄[Fn1][Cra]升高，就該[Fn2]誇耀；
verses.text_en: And let the lowly brother boast in his exaltation,
verses.text_gb_plain: 卑微的弟兄升高，就该夸耀；

footnotes.zh: 雅各在6节用海中的波浪为例，说明疑惑的心；在10节用草上的花描述正在衰残的富足人；这里他用天上薰烤的太阳及其热气为例，说明在神行政的对付之下，人的财富衰残的原因。他在17节甚至用星体的转动为例，说明与父神之不变相对的变动。在三3～12说到舌头的难处时，他用了二十种事物作例证。不仅如此，他在四14，用雾气描述我们生命短暂的出现；在五7～8，用农夫的恒忍教导我们如何等候主来。他是老练的智者，不仅有人生的阅历，也有借祷告从神圣源头求来的智慧(5，三13，17)。然而雅各同情犹太教，与之妥协；这似乎使他受到拦阻，无法透彻看见神新约经纶之智慧的异象，如保罗所看见并在他书信中所揭示的。见三12注1与17注1。
footnotes.zh_big5: 雅各在6節用海中的波浪為例，說明疑惑的心；在10節用草上的花描述正在衰殘的富足人；這裏他用天上薰烤的太陽及其熱氣為例，說明在神行政的對付之下，人的財富衰殘的原因。他在17節甚至用星體的轉動為例，說明與父神之不變相對的變動。在三3～12說到舌頭的難處時，他用了二十種事物作例證。不僅如此，他在四14，用霧氣描述我們生命短暫的出現；在五7～8，用農夫的恆忍教導我們如何等候主來。他是老練的智者，不僅有人生的閱歷，也有藉禱告從神聖源頭求來的智慧。（5，三13，17。）然而雅各同情猶太教，與之妥協；這使他受到攔阻，無法透徹看見神新約經綸之智慧的異象，如保羅所看見並在他書信中所揭示的。見三12註1與17註1。
footnotes.en: 1:11 1 sun In v. 6 James used the surge of the sea to illustrate a doubting heart, and in v. 10 he used the flower of the land to portray the fading rich man. Here he used the sun in the heavens with its scorching heat to illustrate the factor that causes man's riches to fade under God's governmental dealing. In v. 17 he used even the turning of the planets to illustrate variableness, which is in contrast to the invariableness of God the Father. In dealing with the problem of our tongue in James 3:3-12, he used twenty kinds of things for illustrations. Moreover, in James 4:14 he used vapor to portray the brief appearing of our life, and in James 5:7-8 he used the farmer's long-suffering to teach us how to await the Lord's coming. James was a wise and experienced man, having not only the experience of human life but also wisdom from the divine source through his seeking by prayer (v. 5; 3:13, 17). Yet it seems that his sympathy for and compromise with Judaism frustrated him from seeing a thorough vision of the wisdom concerning God's New Testament economy, a vision that Paul saw and unveiled in his Epistles. See note James 3:12 1 and note James 3:17 1 .

footnotes.zh: 对那些追求财富的人，这是何等严肃的话！但对那些失去财富而降卑的富足人，这却是安慰的话。
footnotes.zh_big5: 對那些追求財富的人，這是何等嚴肅的話！但對那些失去財富而降卑的富足人，這卻是安慰的話。
footnotes.en: 1:11 3 rich What a sobering word to those who pursue riches! Yet it is a soothing word to the rich who are being brought low through the loss of their riches.

footnotes.en: 1:12 1 trial Verses James 1:2-12 deal with trials (see note James 1:13 1 ). Trials come from the believers' environment to prove their faith (vv. 2-3) through suffering (vv. 9-11). The believers should endure the trials with all joy (v. 2) because of their love for the Lord, that they may receive the blessing of the crown of life.

footnotes.zh: 即对信徒信心的称许(3)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 即對信徒信心的稱許。（3。）
footnotes.en: 1:12 2 approved I.e., the approving of the believers' faith (v. 3).

footnotes.zh: 这指明12～27节的基础思想，乃是对神生命的急切需要。生我们的父，以及祂生我们，叫我们在祂所造的万物中，成为初熟的果子(17～18，27)，所栽种生命的话(21)，以及完备的生命之律(25)，都证实这点。
footnotes.zh_big5: 本節所說生命的冠冕，和下文所題到生我們的父，並祂生我們，叫我們在祂所造的萬物中，成為初熟的果子，（17～18，27，）以及所栽種的話，（21，）都指向信徒對神聖生命的需要。
footnotes.en: 1:12 3 crown The glory, the expression, of life. The believers endure trials by means of the divine life, and this will become their glory, their expression, the crown of life, as a reward to them at the Lord's appearing, for their enjoyment in the coming kingdom (James 2:5).

footnotes.zh: 指生命的荣耀，生命的彰显。信徒靠着神的生命忍受试炼，这要成为他们的荣耀，他们的彰显，就是生命的冠冕，在主显现时作他们的赏赐，在要来的国度里给他们享受(二5)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 指生命的榮耀，生命的彰顯。信徒靠著神的生命忍受試煉，這要成為他們的榮耀，他們的彰顯，就是生命的冠冕，在主顯現時作他們的賞賜，在要來的國度裏給他們享受。（二5。）
footnotes.en: 1:12 4 life This indicates that the underlying thought in vv. 12-27 is the crucial need of the divine life. The begetting Father and His begetting us, His making us the firstfruits of His creatures (vv. 17-18, 27), the implanted word of life (v. 21), and the perfect law of life (v. 25) all confirm this.

footnotes.zh: 相信主是接受神的生命，使我们得救；爱主是在神的生命里长大成熟，使我们有资格得着生命的冠冕为赏赐，在国度里享受神生命的荣耀。
footnotes.zh_big5: 相信主是接受神的生命，使我們得救；愛主是在神的生命裏長大成熟，使我們有資格得著生命的冠冕為賞賜，在國度裏享受神生命的榮耀。
footnotes.en: 1:12 5 love To believe in the Lord is to receive the divine life for our salvation; to love the Lord is to grow in the divine life for our maturity that we may be qualified for a reward — the crown of life — and enjoy the glory of the divine life in the kingdom.

refs.text_big5: 耶和華阿，你所管教，用律法所教訓的人，是有福的；
refs.text_en: Blessed is the man / Whom You discipline, O Jehovah, / And teach out of Your law;

refs.text_gb: 为义受逼迫的人有福了，因为诸天的国是他们的。
refs.text_big5: 為義受逼迫的人有福了，因為諸天的國是他們的。
refs.text_en: Blessed are those who are persecuted for the sake of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.

refs.text_gb: 人若因我的缘故，辱骂你们，逼迫你们，捏造各样坏话毁谤你们，你们就有福了。
refs.text_big5: 人若因我的緣故，辱罵你們，逼迫你們，捏造各樣壞話毀謗你們，你們就有福了。
refs.text_en: Blessed are you when they reproach and persecute you, and while speaking lies, say every evil thing against you because of Me.

refs.text_gb: 人为人子的缘故，恨恶你们，隔绝你们，辱骂你们，弃掉你们的名，以为是恶，你们就有福了。
refs.text_big5: 人為人子的緣故，恨惡你們，隔絕你們，辱罵你們，棄掉你們的名，以為是惡，你們就有福了。
refs.text_en: Blessed are you when men hate you and when they separate you from them and reproach you and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of Man's sake.

crossrefs.label: b
crossrefs.raw: 启二10，参林前九25，提后四8，彼前五4，启三11

refs.text_gb: 你将要受的苦你不用怕。看哪，魔鬼将要把你们中间几个人下在监里，叫你们受试炼；你们必受患难十日。你务要至死忠信，我就赐给你那生命的冠冕。
refs.text_big5: 你將要受的苦你不用怕。看哪，魔鬼將要把你們中間幾個人下在監裏，叫你們受試煉；你們必受患難十日。你務要至死忠信，我就賜給你那生命的冠冕。
refs.text_en: Do not fear the things that you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to cast some of you into prison that you may be tried, and you will have tribulation for ten days. Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life.

refs.text_gb: 凡较力争胜的，诸事都有节制；他们不过是要得能坏的华冠，我们却是要得不能坏的华冠。
refs.text_big5: 凡較力爭勝的，諸事都有節制；他們不過是要得能壞的華冠，我們卻是要得不能壞的華冠。
refs.text_en: And everyone who contends exercises self-control in all things; they then, that they may receive a corruptible crown, but we, an incorruptible.

refs.text_gb: 从此以后，有公义的冠冕为我存留，就是主，那公义的审判者，在那日要赏赐我的；不但赏赐我，也赏赐凡爱祂显现的人。
refs.text_big5: 從此以後，有公義的冠冕為我存留，就是主，那公義的審判者，在那日要賞賜我的；不但賞賜我，也賞賜凡愛祂顯現的人。
refs.text_en: Henceforth there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, with which the Lord, the righteous Judge, will recompense me in that day, and not only me but also all those who have loved His appearing.

refs.text_gb: 到了牧长显现的时候，你们必得着那不能衰残的荣耀冠冕。
refs.text_big5: 到了牧長顯現的時候，你們必得著那不能衰殘的榮耀冠冕。
refs.text_en: And when the Chief Shepherd is manifested, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.

refs.text_gb: 我必快来，你要持守你所有的，免得有人夺去你的冠冕。
refs.text_big5: 我必快來，你要持守你所有的，免得有人奪去你的冠冕。
refs.text_en: I come quickly; hold fast what you have that no one take your crown.

refs.text_gb: 我亲爱的弟兄们，请听，神岂不是拣选了世上贫穷的人，叫他们在信上富足，并承受祂所应许给那些爱祂之人的国么？
refs.text_big5: 我親愛的弟兄們，請聽，神豈不是揀選了世上貧窮的人，叫他們在信上富足，並承受祂所應許給那些愛祂之人的國麼？
refs.text_en: Listen, my beloved brothers: Did not God choose the poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom, which He promised to those who love Him?

refs.text_gb: 只是如经上所记：“神为爱祂的人所预备的，是眼睛未曾看见，耳朵未曾听见，人心也未曾想到的。”
refs.text_big5: 只是如經上所記：“神為愛祂的人所豫備的，是眼睛未曾看見，耳朵未曾聽見，人心也未曾想到的。”
refs.text_en: But as it is written, "Things which eye has not seen and ear has not heard and which have not come up in man's heart; things which God has prepared for those who love Him."

refs.text_gb: 但若有人爱神，这人乃是神所知道的。
refs.text_big5: 但若有人愛神，這人乃是神所知道的。
refs.text_en: But if anyone loves God, this one is known by Him.

refs.text_gb: 你要全心、全魂、全心思并全力，爱主你的神。”
refs.text_big5: 你要全心、全魂、全心思並全力，愛主你的神。”
refs.text_en: And you shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart and from your whole soul and from your whole mind and from your whole strength."

verses.text_gb: 人[Fn1]被[Cra]试诱，不可说，我是[Fn2]被神试诱，因为神[Fn3]不被恶试诱，祂也[Fn4]不试诱人。
verses.text_big5: 人[Fn1]被[Cra]試誘，不可說，我是[Fn2]被神試誘，因為神[Fn3]不被惡試誘，祂也[Fn4]不試誘人。
verses.text_en: Let no one say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God; for God cannot be tempted of evil, and He Himself tempts no one.
verses.text_gb_plain: 人被试诱，不可说，我是被神试诱，因为神不被恶试诱，祂也不试诱人。
verses.text_big5_plain: 人被試誘，不可說，我是被神試誘，因為神不被惡試誘，祂也不試誘人。

footnotes.zh: 或，被试验，被考验。2、12节的试炼，原文是这里和14节之试诱的名词，这二辞非常相近，都是指试验、考验、验证。被外面环境的苦难试验、考验、验证，乃是试炼(2)；被里面私欲的引诱试验、考验、验证，乃是试诱(14)。2～12节是说到试炼，13～21节是说到试诱。就试炼而言，我们该靠着爱主忍受，好得着祝福——生命的冠冕；就试诱而言，我们该借着领受那栽种的话抵挡，好得着救恩——魂的得救(21)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 或，被試驗，被考驗。2、12節的試煉，原文是這裏和14節之試誘的名詞，這二辭非常相近，都是指試驗、考驗、驗證。被外面環境的苦難試驗、考驗、驗證，乃是試煉；（2；）被裏面私慾的引誘試驗、考驗、驗證，乃是試誘。（14。）2～12節是說到試煉，13～21節是說到試誘。就試煉而言，我們該靠著愛主忍受，好得著祝福─生命的冠冕；就試誘而言，我們該藉著領受那栽種的話抵擋，好得著救恩─魂的得救。（21。）
footnotes.en: 1:13 1 tempted Or, tried, tested. The Greek word for trials and trial in vv. 2, 12 is the noun form of the word for tempted here and in v. 14. The two words are very similar in form; both refer to being tried, tested, proved. To be tried, tested, proved, by outward suffering in the environment is a trial (v. 2). To be tried, tested, proved, by the inward enticing of lust is a temptation (v. 14). The trial is dealt with in vv. 2-12 the temptation is dealt with in vv. 13-21. As for the trial, we should endure it by loving the Lord that we may obtain the blessing — the crown of life. As for the temptation, we should resist it by receiving the implanted word that we may obtain salvation — the salvation of our souls (v. 21).

footnotes.zh: 直译，从神受试诱。
footnotes.zh_big5: 直譯，從神受試誘。
footnotes.en: 1:13 2 of Lit., from.

footnotes.zh: 不被…试诱，原文意，未受试验的，不能试验的；因此是不可试诱的，不被试诱，不能被试诱。
footnotes.zh_big5: 不被…試誘，原文意，未受試驗的，不能試驗的；因此是不可試誘的，不被試誘，不能被試誘。
footnotes.en: 1:13 3 cannot The Greek word means both is untried and is untriable; hence, not temptable, not to be tempted, incapable of being tempted.

footnotes.zh: 那试诱者(太四3，帖前三5)是魔鬼，不是神。
footnotes.zh_big5: 那試誘者（太四3，帖前三5）是魔鬼，不是神。
footnotes.en: 1:13 4 tempts The devil, not God, is the tempter (Matt. 4:3; 1 Thes. 3:5).

refs.text_gb: 不叫我们陷入试诱，救我们脱离那恶者。因为国度、能力、荣耀，都是你的，直到永远。阿们。
refs.text_big5: 不叫我們陷入試誘，救我們脫離那惡者。因為國度、能力、榮耀，都是你的，直到永遠。阿們。
refs.text_en: And do not bring us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For Yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever. Amen.

refs.text_gb: 那临到你们的试诱，无非是人所能受的；神是信实的，必不容你们受试诱过于所能受的，祂也必随着试诱开一条出路，叫你们能忍受得住。
refs.text_big5: 那臨到你們的試誘，無非是人所能受的；神是信實的，必不容你們受試誘過於所能受的，祂也必隨著試誘開一條出路，叫你們能忍受得住。
refs.text_en: No temptation has taken you except that which is common to man; and God is faithful, who will not allow that you be tempted beyond what you are able, but will, with the temptation, also make the way out, that you may be able to endure it.

verses.text_gb: 但各人被试诱，乃是被自己的[Cra]私欲勾引诱惑的；
verses.text_big5: 但各人被試誘，乃是被自己的[Cra]私慾勾引誘惑的；
verses.text_en: But each one is tempted when he is drawn away and enticed by his own lusts;
verses.text_gb_plain: 但各人被试诱，乃是被自己的私欲勾引诱惑的；
verses.text_big5_plain: 但各人被試誘，乃是被自己的私慾勾引誘惑的；

refs.text_gb: 我们众人从前也都在他们中间，在我们肉体的私欲里，行事为人，行肉体和思念所意欲的，生来就是可怒的儿女，和其余的人一样；
refs.text_big5: 我們眾人從前也都在他們中間，在我們肉體的私慾裏，行事為人，行肉體和思念所意欲的，生來就是可怒的兒女，和其餘的人一樣；
refs.text_en: Among whom we also all conducted ourselves once in the lusts of our flesh, doing the desires of the flesh and of the thoughts, and were by nature children of wrath, even as the rest;

verses.text_gb: 然后私欲怀了胎，就[Fn1]生出罪；罪既长成，就产生[Cra]死。
verses.text_big5: 然後私慾懷了胎，就[Fn1]生出罪；罪既長成，就產生[Cra]死。
verses.text_en: Then the lust, having conceived, gives birth to sin; and the sin, when it is fully grown, brings forth death.
verses.text_gb_plain: 然后私欲怀了胎，就生出罪；罪既长成，就产生死。
verses.text_big5_plain: 然後私慾懷了胎，就生出罪；罪既長成，就產生死。

footnotes.zh: 那试诱者魔鬼，是生出罪的父(约壹三8，10)，他借着罪(林前十五56)掌死权(来二14)。他将罪注入亚当里面，死就借着罪遍及众人(罗五12)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 那試誘者魔鬼，是生出罪的父，（約壹三8，10，）他藉著罪（林前十五56）掌死權。（來二14。）他將罪注入亞當裏面，死就藉著罪遍及眾人。（羅五12。）
footnotes.en: 1:15 1 gives The tempter, the devil, is the begetting father of sin (1 John 3:8, 10), having the might of death (Heb. 2:14) through sin (1 Cor. 15:56). He injected sin into Adam, and through sin death passed on to all men (Rom. 5:12).

refs.text_gb: 这就如罪是借着一人入了世界，死又是借着罪来的，于是死就遍及众人，因为众人都犯了罪。
refs.text_big5: 這就如罪是藉著一人入了世界，死又是藉著罪來的，於是死就遍及眾人，因為眾人都犯了罪。
refs.text_en: Therefore just as through one man sin entered into the world, and through sin, death; and thus death passed on to all men because all have sinned-

refs.text_gb: 那时你们有什么果子？不过是你们现今所看为羞耻的事，那些事的结局就是死。
refs.text_big5: 那時你們有甚麼果子？不過是你們現今所看為羞恥的事，那些事的結局就是死。
refs.text_en: What fruit then did you have at that time? Things of which you are now ashamed, for the end of those things is death.

refs.text_gb: 因为罪的工价乃是死，唯有神的恩赐，在我们的主基督耶稣里，乃是永远的生命。
refs.text_big5: 因為罪的工價乃是死，惟有神的恩賜，在我們的主基督耶穌裏，乃是永遠的生命。
refs.text_en: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

verses.text_gb: 我亲爱的弟兄们，不要看错了。
verses.text_big5: 我親愛的弟兄們，不要看錯了。
verses.text_en: Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.
verses.text_gb_plain: 我亲爱的弟兄们，不要看错了。
verses.text_big5_plain: 我親愛的弟兄們，不要看錯了。

verses.text_gb: 一切美善的[Fn1]赐与、和各样完备的[Cra]恩赐，都是从[Crb]上头，从[Fn2]众光之父降下来的，在祂并[Crc]没有[Fn3]变动，或转动的影儿。
verses.text_big5: 一切美善的[Fn1]賜與、和各樣完備的[Cra]恩賜，都是從[Crb]上頭，從[Fn2]眾光之父降下來的，在祂並[Crc]沒有[Fn3]變動，或轉動的影兒。
verses.text_en: All good giving and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variation or shadow cast by turning.
verses.text_gb_plain: 一切美善的赐与、和各样完备的恩赐，都是从上头，从众光之父降下来的，在祂并没有变动，或转动的影儿。
verses.text_big5_plain: 一切美善的賜與、和各樣完備的恩賜，都是從上頭，從眾光之父降下來的，在祂並沒有變動，或轉動的影兒。

footnotes.zh: 赐与是指给与的行动，恩赐是指给与的东西。
footnotes.en: 1:17 1 giving; gift Giving refers to the act of giving; gift refers to the thing given.

footnotes.zh: 这里的众光是指天上的光体，父是这些发光体的创造者、源头。在祂并没有转动的影儿，不像天上的星体有转动投射的影儿，如月亮因绕转而有盈亏，或日蚀时太阳被月亮所遮；因祂不变动，也不转变。既是这样，祂就不能被恶试诱，也不试诱任何人。
footnotes.zh_big5: 這裏的眾光是指天上的光體，父是這些發光體的創造者、源頭。在祂並沒有轉動的影兒，不像天上的星體有轉動投射的影兒，如月亮因繞轉而有盈虧，或日蝕時太陽被月亮所遮；因祂不變動，也不轉變。既是這樣，祂就不能被惡試誘，也不試誘任何人。
footnotes.en: 1:17 2 Father Lights here refers to the heavenly luminaries. The Father is the Creator, the source, of these shining bodies. With Him there is no shadow cast by turning (in contrast to the situation with the heavenly orbs, where the moon waxes and wanes by its revolving, and the sun can be eclipsed by the moon), for He is not variable, not changeable. As such, He is incapable of being tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone.

footnotes.zh: 或，可变性。
footnotes.zh_big5: 或，可變性。
footnotes.en: 1:17 3 variation Or, variableness.

refs.text_gb: 耶和华必赐下好处，我们的地要多出土产。
refs.text_big5: 耶和華必賜下好處，我們的地要多出土產。
refs.text_en: Indeed Jehovah will give what is good, / And our land will give its increase.

refs.text_gb: 约翰回答说，若不是从天上赐的，人就不能得到什么。
refs.text_big5: 約翰回答說，若不是從天上賜的，人就不能得到甚麼。
refs.text_en: John answered and said, A man cannot receive anything unless it has been given to him from heaven.

refs.text_gb: 这样的智慧，不是从上头下来的，乃是属地的、属魂的、出于鬼且像鬼的。
refs.text_big5: 這樣的智慧，不是從上頭下來的，乃是屬地的、屬魂的、出於鬼且像鬼的。
refs.text_en: This wisdom is not that which descends from above, but is earthly, soulish, demonic.

refs.text_gb: 耶稣对他们说，你们是出于下头的，我是出于上头的；你们是属这世界的，我不是属这世界的。
refs.text_big5: 耶穌對他們說，你們是出於下頭的，我是出於上頭的；你們是屬這世界的，我不是屬這世界的。
refs.text_en: And He said to them, You are from below, I am from above; you are of this world, I am not of this world.

refs.text_gb: 唯有你仍是一样，你的年数也没有穷尽。
refs.text_big5: 惟有你仍是一樣，你的年數也沒有窮盡。
refs.text_en: But You are the same, / And Your years are without end.

refs.text_gb: 因我耶和华是不改变的；所以雅各的子孙哪，你们没有灭亡。
refs.text_big5: 因我耶和華是不改變的；所以雅各的子孫哪，你們沒有滅亡。
refs.text_en: For I, Jehovah, do not change; therefore you, O sons of Jacob, are not consumed.

verses.text_gb: 祂照自己的[Fn1]定意，用[Fn2][Cra]真理的话[Fn3][Crb]生了我们，叫我们在祂所造的万物中，成为[Fn4][Crc]初熟的果子。
verses.text_big5: 祂照自己的[Fn1]定意，用[Fn2][Cra]真理的話[Fn3][Crb]生了我們，叫我們在祂所造的萬物中，成為[Fn4][Crc]初熟的果子。
verses.text_en: He brought us forth by the word of truth, purposing that we might be a kind of firstfruits of His creatures.
verses.text_gb_plain: 祂照自己的定意，用真理的话生了我们，叫我们在祂所造的万物中，成为初熟的果子。
verses.text_big5_plain: 祂照自己的定意，用真理的話生了我們，叫我們在祂所造的萬物中，成為初熟的果子。

footnotes.zh: 这定意是出于祂自己的旨意，借着祂的意愿，要借着生我们，叫我们在祂所造的万物中，成为初熟的果子，以完成祂的定旨。
footnotes.zh_big5: 這定意是出於祂自己的旨意，藉著祂的意願，要藉著生我們，叫我們在祂所造的萬物中，成為初熟的果子，以完成祂的定旨。
footnotes.en: 1:18 1 brought Sin, the source of darkness, brings forth death (v. 15). But the Father of lights brought us forth to be the firstfruits of His creatures, full of the vigorous life that matures first. This refers to the divine birth, our regeneration (John 3:5, 6), which is carried out according to God's eternal purpose.

footnotes.zh: 这是神圣实际的话，就是三一神所是的话(约一14，17)；这话乃是生命的种子，借此我们蒙了重生(彼前一23)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 這是神聖實際的話，就是三一神所是的話；（約一14，17；）這話乃是生命的種子，藉此我們蒙了重生。（彼前一23。）
footnotes.en: 1:18 2 word The word of the divine reality, of what the Triune God is (John 1:14, 17). This word is the seed of life, by which we have been regenerated (1 Pet. 1:23).

footnotes.zh: 黑暗的源头，罪，产生死(15)，但众光之父生了我们，叫我们在祂所造的万物中，成为初熟的果子，满了旺盛、首先成熟的生命。这是指神圣的出生，就是我们的重生(约三5～6)，是照着神永远的定旨完成在我们身上的。
footnotes.zh_big5: 黑暗的源頭，罪，產生死，（15，）但眾光之父生了我們，叫我們在祂所造的萬物中，成為初熟的果子，滿了旺盛、首先成熟的生命。這是指神聖的出生，就是我們的重生，（約三5～6，）是照著神永遠的定旨完成在我們身上的。
footnotes.en: 1:18 3 purposing Of His own will, by His intention, to carry out His purpose by begetting us that we may become the firstfruits of His creatures.

footnotes.zh: 直译，一种初熟的果子。神要更新祂的整个创造，好得着以新耶路撒冷为中心的新天新地(启二一1～2)。首先祂借所栽种生命的话，将祂神圣的生命分赐到我们里面，重生我们作祂新造中初熟的果子，使我们过完全的生活。这该是基督徒实行之完全的种子。这生命要终结于神永远的新宇宙中那活的中心，新耶路撒冷。
footnotes.zh_big5: 直譯，一種初熟的果子。神要更新祂的整個創造，好得著以新耶路撒冷為中心的新天新地。（啟二一1～2。）首先祂將祂神聖的生命分賜到我們裏面，重生我們作祂新造中初熟的果子，使我們過完全的生活。這該是基督徒實行之完全的種子。這生命要終結於神永遠的新宇宙中那活的中心，新耶路撒冷。
footnotes.en: 1:18 4 firstfruits God will renew His entire creation to have a new heaven and new earth with the New Jerusalem as the center (Rev. 21:1-2). He first regenerated us to be the firstfruits of His new creation by imparting His divine life into our being through the implanted word of life that we might live a life of perfection. This must be the seed of practical Christian perfection. This life will consummate in the New Jerusalem as the living center of God's eternal new universe.

refs.text_gb: 但你们心里若怀着苦毒的嫉妒和私图好争，就不要再夸口，也不要再说谎抵挡真理了。
refs.text_big5: 但你們心裏若懷著苦毒的嫉妒和私圖好爭，就不要再誇口，也不要再說謊抵擋真理了。
refs.text_en: But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, do not boast and lie against the truth.

refs.text_gb: 我的弟兄们，你们中间若有人受迷惑离开真理，有人使他回转，
refs.text_big5: 我的弟兄們，你們中間若有人受迷惑離開真理，有人使他回轉，
refs.text_en: My brothers, if any one among you is led astray from the truth and someone turns him back,

refs.text_gb: 我们主耶稣基督的神与父是当受颂赞的，祂曾照自己的大怜悯，借耶稣基督从死人中复活，重生了我们，使我们有活的盼望，
refs.text_big5: 我們主耶穌基督的神與父是當受頌讚的，祂曾照自己的大憐憫，藉耶穌基督從死人中復活，重生了我們，使我們有活的盼望，
refs.text_en: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to His great mercy has regenerated us unto a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,

refs.text_gb: 你们蒙了重生，不是由于能坏的种子，乃是由于不能坏的种子，是借着神活而常存的话。
refs.text_big5: 你們蒙了重生，不是由於能壞的種子，乃是由於不能壞的種子，是藉著神活而常存的話。
refs.text_en: Having been regenerated not of corruptible seed but of incorruptible, through the living and abiding word of God.

refs.text_gb: 这等人不是从血生的，不是从肉体的意思生的，也不是从人的意思生的，乃是从神生的。
refs.text_big5: 這等人不是從血生的，不是從肉體的意思生的，也不是從人的意思生的，乃是從神生的。
refs.text_en: Who were begotten not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

refs.text_gb: 你们若晓得祂是义的，就当知道凡行义的人也都是从祂生的。
refs.text_big5: 你們若曉得祂是義的，就當知道凡行義的人也都是從祂生的。
refs.text_en: If you know that He is righteous, you know that everyone who practices righteousness also has been begotten of Him.

refs.text_gb: 凡从神生的，就不犯罪，因为神的种子住在他里面；他也不能犯罪，因为他是从神生的。
refs.text_big5: 凡從神生的，就不犯罪，因為神的種子住在他裏面；他也不能犯罪，因為他是從神生的。
refs.text_en: Everyone who has been begotten of God does not practice sin, because His seed abides in him; and he cannot sin, because he has been begotten of God.

refs.text_gb: 凡信耶稣是基督的，都是从神生的；凡爱那生他的，也爱从祂生的。
refs.text_big5: 凡信耶穌是基督的，都是從神生的；凡愛那生他的，也愛從祂生的。
refs.text_en: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been begotten of God, and everyone who loves Him who has begotten loves him also who has been begotten of Him.

refs.text_gb: 我们晓得凡从神生的都不犯罪，那从神生的，保守自己，那恶者也就不摸他。
refs.text_big5: 我們曉得凡從神生的都不犯罪，那從神生的，保守自己，那惡者也就不摸他。
refs.text_en: We know that everyone who is begotten of God does not sin, but he who has been begotten of God keeps himself, and the evil one does not touch him.

refs.text_gb: 那时以色列归耶和华为圣，作为祂所出产的初熟果子；凡吞吃他的，便算为有罪，灾祸就临到他们；这是耶和华说的。
refs.text_big5: 那時以色列歸耶和華為聖，作為祂所出產的初熟果子；凡吞喫他的，便算為有罪，災禍就臨到他們；這是耶和華說的。
refs.text_en: Israel was holiness to Jehovah, / The firstfruits of His increase; / All who ate of it were guilty; / Evil came upon them, / Declares Jehovah.

refs.text_gb: 这些人未曾与妇女在一起受到玷污，他们原是童身。羔羊无论往哪里去，他们都跟随祂。他们是从人间买来的，作初熟的果子归与神和羔羊；
refs.text_big5: 這些人未曾與婦女在一起受到玷污，他們原是童身。羔羊無論往那裏去，他們都跟隨祂。他們是從人間買來的，作初熟的果子歸與神和羔羊；
refs.text_en: These are they who have not been defiled with women, for they are virgins. These are they who follow the Lamb wherever He may go. These were purchased from among men as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb.

verses.text_gb: 我亲爱的弟兄们，这是你们[Fn1]所知道的，但你们各人要快快地听，[Fn2]慢慢地[Cra]说，慢慢地[Crb]动怒；
verses.text_big5: 我親愛的弟兄們，這是你們[Fn1]所知道的，但你們各人要快快的聽，[Fn2]慢慢的[Cra]說，慢慢的[Crb]動怒；
verses.text_en: You know this, my beloved brothers; but let every man be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath;
verses.text_gb_plain: 我亲爱的弟兄们，这是你们所知道的，但你们各人要快快地听，慢慢地说，慢慢地动怒；
verses.text_big5_plain: 我親愛的弟兄們，這是你們所知道的，但你們各人要快快的聽，慢慢的說，慢慢的動怒；

footnotes.zh: 或，要知道的。
footnotes.zh_big5: 或，要知道的。
footnotes.en: 1:19 1 You Or, Know this.

footnotes.zh: 听，试诱我们说；而说，乃是那点起忿怒的火(参三6)。我们若勒住自己不说(参26)，就能平息忿怒。雅各在这里的话，乃为加强他对基督徒实行之完全的观点，语调很像旧约的箴言(箴十19，十四17)。
footnotes.zh_big5: 聽，試誘我們說；而說，乃是那點起忿怒的火。（參三6。）我們若勒住自己不說，（參26，）就能平息忿怒。雅各在這裏的話，乃為加強他對基督徒實行之完全的觀點，語調很像舊約的箴言。（箴十19，十四17。）
footnotes.en: 1:19 2 slow Hearing tempts us to speak, and speaking is the fire that kindles wrath (cf. James 3:6). If we bridle our speaking (cf. v. 26), we will quench our wrath. James's word here, given to strengthen his view of practical Christian perfection, has the tone of the Old Testament proverbs (Prov. 10:19; 14:17).

refs.text_gb: 你在神面前不可冒失开口，也不可心急发言；因为神在天上，你在地上，所以你的言语要寡少。
refs.text_big5: 你在神面前不可冒失開口，也不可心急發言；因為神在天上，你在地上，所以你的言語要寡少。
refs.text_en: Do not be rash with your mouth, and let not your heart hastily utter anything before God; for God is in heaven and you are on the earth; therefore let your words be few.

refs.text_gb: 急躁易怒的，行事愚昧；设诡计的，被人恨恶。
refs.text_big5: 急躁易怒的，行事愚昧；設詭計的，被人恨惡。
refs.text_en: He who is quick to anger will deal foolishly, / And a man of wicked devices is hated.

refs.text_gb: 不轻易发怒的，大有聪明；灵里暴躁的，大显愚妄。
refs.text_big5: 不輕易發怒的，大有聰明；靈裏暴躁的，大顯愚妄。
refs.text_en: He who is slow to anger is of great understanding, / But he who has a hasty spirit exalts folly.

refs.text_gb: 不轻易发怒的，胜过勇士；治服己灵的，强如取城。
refs.text_big5: 不輕易發怒的，勝過勇士；治服己靈的，強如取城。
refs.text_en: He who is slow to anger is better than the mighty; / And he who rules his spirit, than he who captures a city.

refs.text_gb: 你不要灵里急躁恼怒，因为恼怒存在愚昧人的怀中。
refs.text_big5: 你不要靈裏急躁惱怒，因為惱怒存在愚昧人的懷中。
refs.text_en: Do not be quick in your spirit to become angry, / For anger rests in the bosom of fools.

verses.text_gb: 因为[Fn1]人的忿怒并不成就神的义。
verses.text_big5: 因為[Fn1]人的忿怒並不成就神的義。
verses.text_en: For the wrath of man does not accomplish the righteousness of God.
verses.text_gb_plain: 因为人的忿怒并不成就神的义。
verses.text_big5_plain: 因為人的忿怒並不成就神的義。

footnotes.zh: 神的义无需人的忿怒帮助；要成就神的义，人的忿怒是无用的。
footnotes.zh_big5: 神的義無需人的忿怒幫助；要成就神的義，人的忿怒是無用的。
footnotes.en: 1:20 1 wrath The righteousness of God does not need the help of man's wrath, which is of no use in the carrying out of God's righteousness.

verses.text_gb: 所以你们既[Cra]脱去一切的[Crb]污秽，和盈余的恶毒，就该用[Crc]温柔领受那[Fn1]栽种的[Crd]话，就是能[Fn2]救你们魂的话。
verses.text_big5: 所以你們既[Cra]脫去一切的[Crb]污穢，和盈餘的惡毒，就該用[Crc]溫柔領受那[Fn1]栽種的[Crd]話，就是能[Fn2]救你們魂的話。
verses.text_en: Therefore putting away all filthiness and the abundance of malice, receive in meekness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
verses.text_gb_plain: 所以你们既脱去一切的污秽，和盈余的恶毒，就该用温柔领受那栽种的话，就是能救你们魂的话。
verses.text_big5_plain: 所以你們既脫去一切的污穢，和盈餘的惡毒，就該用溫柔領受那栽種的話，就是能救你們魂的話。

footnotes.zh: 这里将神的话比作有生命的植物，栽种到我们里面，并在我们里面长大、结果，使我们的魂得救。我们需要用温柔，用全般的服从，领受神这话，毫不抗拒。
footnotes.zh_big5: 這裏將神的話比作有生命的植物，栽種到我們裏面，並在我們裏面長大、結果，使我們的魂得救。我們需要用溫柔，用全般的服從，領受神這話，毫不抗拒。
footnotes.en: 1:21 1 implanted This likens the word of God to a living plant that is planted into our being and grows in us to bring forth fruit for the salvation of our souls. We need to receive such a word in meekness, in all submission, without any resistance.

footnotes.zh: 按本章全文看，魂的得救包含忍受环境的试炼(2～12)，并抗拒私欲的试诱(13～21)。雅各对魂得救的看法有点消极，不像保罗那样积极；保罗说，我们的魂能借着那更新人的灵得着变化，甚至变成主的形像，从荣耀到荣耀(罗十二2，弗四23，林后三18)。见彼前一5注6，来十39注3。
footnotes.zh_big5: 按本章全文看，魂的得救包含忍受環境的試煉，（2～12，）並抗拒私慾的試誘。（13～21。）雅各對魂得救的看法有點消極，不像保羅那樣積極；保羅說，我們的魂能藉著那更新人的靈得著變化，甚至變成主的形像，從榮耀到榮耀。（羅十二2，弗四23，林後三18。）見彼前一5註6，來十39註3。
footnotes.en: 1:21 2 save The salvation of our souls, according to the context of this chapter, implies the enduring of trials raised up by the environment (vv. 2-12) and the resisting of the temptation of lust (vv. 13-21). James's view concerning the salvation of our souls was somewhat negative and was not as positive as that of Paul, who said that our soul can be transformed by the renewing Spirit, even into the image of the Lord from glory to glory (Rom. 12:2; Eph. 4:23; 2 Cor. 3:18). See note 1 Pet. 1:5 5 and note Heb. 10:39 3 .

refs.text_gb: 在从前的生活样式上，脱去了旧人，这旧人是照着那迷惑的情欲败坏的；
refs.text_big5: 在從前的生活樣式上，脫去了舊人，這舊人是照著那迷惑的情慾敗壞的；
refs.text_en: That you put off, as regards your former manner of life, the old man, which is being corrupted according to the lusts of the deceit,

refs.text_gb: 所以，我们既有这许多的见证人，如同云彩围着我们，就当脱去各样的重担，和容易缠累我们的罪，凭着忍耐奔那摆在我们前头的赛程，
refs.text_big5: 所以，我們既有這許多的見證人，如同雲彩圍著我們，就當脫去各樣的重擔，和容易纏累我們的罪，憑著忍耐奔那擺在我們前頭的賽程，
refs.text_en: Therefore let us also, having so great a cloud of witnesses surrounding us, put away every encumbrance and the sin which so easily entangles us and run with endurance the race which is set before us,

refs.text_gb: 所以亲爱的，我们既有这些应许，就当洁净自己，除去肉身和灵一切的玷污，敬畏神，以成全圣别。
refs.text_big5: 所以親愛的，我們既有這些應許，就當潔淨自己，除去肉身和靈一切的玷污，敬畏神，以成全聖別。
refs.text_en: Therefore since we have these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and of spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

refs.text_gb: 你们中间谁是有智慧有见识的？他就当用智慧的温柔，凭他美好的品行，显出他所作所为的。
refs.text_big5: 你們中間誰是有智慧有見識的？他就當用智慧的溫柔，憑他美好的品行，顯出他所作所為的。
refs.text_en: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his good manner of life his works in meekness of wisdom.

refs.text_gb: 温柔的人有福了，因为他们必承受地土。
refs.text_big5: 溫柔的人有福了，因為他們必承受地土。
refs.text_en: Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.

refs.text_gb: 你们蒙了重生，不是由于能坏的种子，乃是由于不能坏的种子，是借着神活而常存的话。
refs.text_big5: 你們蒙了重生，不是由於能壞的種子，乃是由於不能壞的種子，是藉著神活而常存的話。
refs.text_en: Having been regenerated not of corruptible seed but of incorruptible, through the living and abiding word of God.

refs.text_gb: 凡听见国度之道不领悟的，那恶者就来，把撒在他心里的夺了去；这就是那撒在路旁的。
refs.text_big5: 凡聽見國度之道不領悟的，那惡者就來，把撒在他心裏的奪了去；這就是那撒在路旁的。
refs.text_en: When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand, the evil one comes and snatches away that which has been sown in his heart. This is the one sown beside the way.

refs.text_gb: 但那撒在好土里的，就是人听了道，也领悟了，他就结出果实，有的结了一百倍，有的六十倍，有的三十倍。
refs.text_big5: 但那撒在好土裏的，就是人聽了道，也領悟了，他就結出果實，有的結了一百倍，有的六十倍，有的三十倍。
refs.text_en: But the one sown on the good earth, this is he who hears the word and understands, who by all means bears fruit and produces, one a hundredfold, and one sixtyfold, and one thirtyfold.

verses.text_gb: 只是你们要作[Cra]行[Fn1]道者，不要单作[Crb]听道者，自己[Crc]欺哄自己。
verses.text_big5: 只是你們要作[Cra]行[Fn1]道者，不要單作[Crb]聽道者，自己[Crc]欺哄自己。
verses.text_en: And become doers of the word and not hearers only, who delude themselves.
verses.text_gb_plain: 只是你们要作行道者，不要单作听道者，自己欺哄自己。
verses.text_big5_plain: 只是你們要作行道者，不要單作聽道者，自己欺哄自己。

footnotes.zh: 同前节的“话。”下节者同。

refs.text_gb: 我的弟兄们，若有人说自己有信心，却没有行为，有什么益处？难道这信心能救他么？
refs.text_big5: 我的弟兄們，若有人說自己有信心，卻沒有行為，有甚麼益處？難道這信心能救他麼？
refs.text_en: What is the profit, my brothers, if anyone says he has faith but does not have works? Can that faith save him?

refs.text_gb: 若有弟兄或姊妹经常是赤身露体的，又缺了日用的食物，
refs.text_big5: 若有弟兄或姊妹經常是赤身露體的，又缺了日用的食物，
refs.text_en: If a brother or sister is without clothing and lacks daily food,

refs.text_gb: 而你们中间有人对他们说，平平安安地去吧，愿你们穿得暖，吃得饱；却不给他们身体所需用的，有什么益处？
refs.text_big5: 而你們中間有人對他們說，平平安安的去罷，願你們穿得暖，喫得飽；卻不給他們身體所需用的，有甚麼益處？
refs.text_en: And any one of you says to them, Go in peace, be warmed and filled, yet you do not give them the necessities of the body, what is the profit?

refs.text_gb: 信心也是这样，若没有行为，就是死的。
refs.text_big5: 信心也是這樣，若沒有行為，就是死的。
refs.text_en: So also faith, if it does not have works, is dead in itself.

refs.text_gb: 有人会说，你有信心，我有行为；你将你没有行为的信心指给我看，我便由我的行为，将我的信心指给你看。
refs.text_big5: 有人會說，你有信心，我有行為；你將你沒有行為的信心指給我看，我便由我的行為，將我的信心指給你看。
refs.text_en: But someone will say, You have faith, and I have works; show me your faith without the works, and I will show you my faith by my works.

refs.text_gb: 你信神只有一位；你信的不错；鬼也信，却是战惊。
refs.text_big5: 你信神只有一位；你信的不錯；鬼也信，卻是戰驚。
refs.text_en: You believe that God is one. You do well; the demons also believe and shudder.

refs.text_gb: 虚浮的人哪，你愿意知道没有行为的信心是无用的么？
refs.text_big5: 虛浮的人哪，你願意知道沒有行為的信心是無用的麼？

footnotes.zh: 雅各在此说到摩西的律法是“完备自由的律法。”（参二12。）他使用这辞，也许是根据诗十九7～8，那里说到律法是完全的，能苏醒人的魂，亦即使人得自由，且能快活人心，含示释放与自由；并根据诗一一九11，那里说到将律法存在心中能使我们脱离罪。雅各高举旧约字句的律法到极点，将神新约的经纶与过时的旧约经纶搀混在一起。（徒二一18～20。）他认为律法是基督徒完全的主要凭借。反之，使徒保罗说，律法不能作什么，使我们得完全。（来七19，参加三3。）参二12注1。 在神新约的经纶中，基督已经了结律法；（罗十4，来十9；）信徒已经蒙基督释放，脱离律法奴役的轭，（加五1，）已经向律法死了，（加二19，）并且不再在律法之下，乃在恩典之下。（罗六14，参约一17。）再者，那写在我们外面石版上字句的律法，已经被写在我们心上生命的律法(来八10)，顶替，后者的道德标准符合主在山上颁布的国度宪法(太五～七)。字句的律法不能赐人生命(加三21)，只能暴露人的软弱、失败，将人留在奴役里(加五1与注4)，因此是辖制的律法。生命之律乃是我们重生时分赐到我们里面之神生命的功用，且在我们基督徒的一生中，用神生命追测不尽的丰富供应我们，释放我们，使我们脱离罪与死的律，并成就字句律法一切义的要求(罗八2，4)，因此该视为自由的律法。这律法就是基督的律法(林前九21)，甚至是基督自己，活在我们里面，借着将神的性情分赐到我们里面，规律我们，使我们能过彰显神形像的生活。这律法才该被视为基督徒生活达到实行之完全的基本法则。
footnotes.zh_big5: 雅各在此說到摩西的律法是“完備自由的律法。”（參二12。）他使用這辭，也許是根據詩十九7～8，那裏說到律法是完全的，能甦醒人的魂，亦即使人得自由，且能快活人心，含示釋放與自由；並根據詩一一九11，那裏說到將律法存在心中能使我們脫離罪。雅各高舉舊約字句的律法到極點，將神新約的經綸與過時的舊約經綸攙混在一起。（徒二一18～20。）他認為律法是基督徒完全的主要憑藉。反之，使徒保羅說，律法不能作甚麼，使我們得完全。（來七19，參加三3。）參二12註1。ˍ在神新約的經綸中，基督已經了結律法；（羅十4，來十9；）信徒已經蒙基督釋放，脫離律法奴役的軛，（加五1，）已經向律法死了，（加二19，）並且不再在律法之下，乃在恩典之下。（羅六14，參約一17。）再者，那寫在我們外面石版上字句的律法，已經被寫在我們心上生命的律法（來八10）頂替，後者的道德標準符合主在山上頒佈的國度憲法。（太五～七。）字句的律法不能賜人生命，（加三21，）只能暴露人的軟弱、失敗，將人留在奴役裏，（加五1與註4，）因此是轄制的律法。生命之律乃是我們重生時分賜到我們裏面之神生命的功用，且在我們基督徒的一生中，用神生命追測不盡的豐富供應我們，釋放我們，使我們脫離罪與死的律，並成就字句律法一切義的要求，（羅八2，4，）因此該視為自由的律法。這律法就是基督的律法，（林前九21，）甚至是基督自己，活在我們裏面，藉著將神的性情分賜到我們裏面，規律我們，使我們能過彰顯神形像的生活。這律法纔該被視為基督徒生活達到實行之完全的基本法則。
footnotes.en: 1:25 2 perfect Here James refers to the Mosaic law as "the perfect law, the law of freedom (or liberty)" (cf. 2:12). His use of this expression might have been based on Psa. 19:7-8, which says that the law is perfect, that it restores the soul, i.e., gives people freedom, and that it makes the heart joyous, implying release and freedom, and on Psa. 119:11, which says that keeping the law in our hearts frees us from sin. James uplifted the Old Testament law of letters to the uttermost, mixing God’s New Testament economy with the outdated Old Testament economy (Acts 21:18-20). In his consideration the law was a primary means of Christian perfection. In contrast, the apostle Paul said that the law can do nothing to perfect us (Heb. 7:19; cf. Gal. 3:3). Cf. note 12 2 in ch. 2. In God’s New Testament dispensation Christ has ended the law (Rom. 10:4; Heb. 10:9), and the believers have been freed by Christ from the yoke of slavery of the law (Gal. 5:1), have died to the law (Gal. 2:19), and are no longer under the law but under grace (Rom. 6:14; cf. John 1:17). Moreover, the law of letters written on tablets of stone outside us has been replaced by the law of life inscribed on our hearts (Heb. 8:10), the moral standard of which corresponds with that of the kingdom’s constitution, decreed by the Lord on the mount (Matt. 5—7). Since the law of letters was not able to give man life (Gal. 3:21) but was able only to expose man’s weakness and failure and keep him in slavery (Gal. 5:1 and note 4), it was a law of bondage. Since the law of life is the function of the divine life, which was imparted into our being at regeneration and supplies us throughout our Christian life with the unsearchable riches of the divine life to free us from the law of sin and death and fulfill all the righteous requirements of the law of letters (Rom. 8:2, 4), it should be considered the law of freedom. This law is the law of Christ (1 Cor. 9:21), even Christ Himself, who lives within us to regulate us by imparting the divine nature into our being, that we may live a life that expresses God’s image. It is this law that should be considered the basic rule of the Christian life for practical Christian perfection.

footnotes.zh: “虔敬的”是形容词，名词是“虔敬，”原文指礼拜的仪式和对神的敬拜(含对神的敬畏)。形容词只在这里用到，名词在这里和27节是用在积极的意义上，在西二18(敬拜)是用在消极的意义上，在徒二六5(宗教)是用在一般的意义上。关于神新约的经纶，雅各所写的，不如保罗、彼得、约翰那样显著。保罗专注于基督活在我们里面，并成形在我们里面(加二20，四19)，基督在我们身上显大，并从我们身上活出来(腓一20～21)，使我们，就是召会，祂的身体，能成为祂的丰满，祂的彰显(弗一22～23)。彼得强调神借着基督的复活重生了我们(彼前一3)，使我们有分于神的性情，叫我们过敬虔的生活(彼后一3～7)，并且被建造成为属灵的殿，彰显祂的美德(彼前二5，9)。约翰强调我们所得永远的生命，使我们与三一神有交通(约壹一2～3)，以及神圣的出生，将神圣的生命带进我们里面，作神圣的种子，叫我们活出像神的生活(约壹二29，三9，四17)，并且成为召会，就是灯台，为耶稣作见证(启一9，11～12)，将来要终结于新耶路撒冷，彰显神直到永远(启二一2～3，10～11)。雅各所强调，那像是新约特征的，不过是神生了我们(18)，完备自由的律法(25)，内住的灵(四5)，以及稍微提到召会(五14)。他没有说到基督是我们的生命，召会是基督的彰显，这两个新约中最特出、最具时代的特征。照本书看，雅各必定非常虔敬。也许由于这点，以及他在基督徒实行上的完全，使他与彼得、约翰同被称为在耶路撒冷召会的柱石，甚至在其中为首(加二9)。然而，就着神在基督里新约经纶的启示说，他却不强，反倒仍在旧犹太宗教背景的影响之下，凭着礼仪敬拜神，并过敬畏神的生活。他在徒二一20～24和本书二2～11的话，都证实这点。他属灵的眼光受了犹太教的笼罩，不能完全进入神新约经纶的启示，像保罗、彼得、约翰那样。
footnotes.en: 1:26 1 religious; religion In Greek, religious (adjective) and religion (noun) refer to ceremonial service and worship to God (implying the fear of God). The adjective is used only here. The noun is used in a positive sense here and in v. 27, in a negative sense in Col. 2:18 (for worship), and in a general sense in Acts 26:5. James's writing concerning God's New Testament economy is not as striking as Paul's, Peter's, and John's. Paul focuses on Christ living and being formed in us (Gal. 2:20; 4:19) and Christ being magnified in us and lived out of us (Phil. 1:20-21) that we as the church, His Body, may become His fullness, His expression (Eph. 1:22-23). Peter stresses the fact that God regenerated us through the resurrection of Christ (1 Pet. 1:3), making us partakers of His divine nature, that we may live a life of godliness (2 Pet. 1:3-7) and be built up as a spiritual house to express His virtues (1 Pet. 2:5, 9). John emphasizes the eternal life, given to us for our fellowship with the Triune God (1 John 1:2-3), and the divine birth, which brings into us the divine life as the divine seed that we may live out a life that is like God (1 John 2:29; 3:9; 4:17) and be the church, a lampstand, which bears the testimony of Jesus (Rev. 1:9, 11-12) and which will consummate in the New Jerusalem for God's expression unto eternity (Rev. 21:2-3, 10-11). Of the matters that are characteristic of the New Testament, James stresses only God's begetting of us (v. 18), the perfect law of freedom (v. 25), the indwelling Spirit (James 4:5), and a minor aspect of the church (James 5:14). He does not speak of Christ as our life or of the church as the expression of Christ, the two most outstanding and dispensational characteristics of the New Testament. This Epistle shows that James must have been very religious. It might have been because of this and his practical Christian perfection that he was reputed to be, along with Peter and John, a pillar, even the first, in the church at Jerusalem (Gal. 2:9). However, he was not strong in the revelation of God's New Testament economy in Christ but was still under the influence of the background of the old Judaic religion, the primary elements of which were to worship God by ceremonies and to live a life in the fear of God. This is proved by the words in Acts 21:20-24 and in Acts 2:2-11 of this Epistle. Because his spiritual sight was covered by Judaism, he could not fully enter into the revelation of God's New Testament economy as Paul, Peter, and John were able to do.

footnotes.zh: 不勒住舌头，就是说话又快(参19)又随便，没有节制。这常欺骗说话者的心，欺骗他的良心，就是他心里的知觉。

footnotes.en: 1:26 2 not Not to bridle the tongue is to speak quickly (cf. v. 19) and loosely without restriction. This always deceives the speaking one's own heart, deceiving his conscience — the consciousness of his heart.

footnotes.zh_big5: 雅各這話乃是為加強他對基督徒實行之完全的觀點，其中含有舊約命令的成分。（申十四29，二四19～21，12～13。）
footnotes.en: 1:27 1 orphans In this word of James's, given to strengthen his view of practical Christian perfection, an element of the Old Testament charges is implied (Deut. 14:29; 12-13, 24:19-21).

footnotes.zh: 即不世俗化、不被世俗沾染。这也是雅各对基督徒实行的完全，因敬畏神而有的部分观点。看顾孤儿寡妇是照着神的爱心行事，乃是基督徒的完全积极一面的特征；保守自己不受世界玷污，是照着神圣别的性情，从世界圣别出来，乃是基督徒的完全消极一面的特征。
footnotes.zh_big5: 即不世俗化、不被世俗沾染。這也是雅各對基督徒實行的完全，因敬畏神而有的部分觀點。看顧孤兒寡婦是照著神的愛心行事，乃是基督徒的完全積極一面的特徵；保守自己不受世界玷污，是照著神聖別的性情，從世界聖別出來，乃是基督徒的完全消極一面的特徵。
footnotes.en: 1:27 2 unspotted Not to be worldly, not to be stained by worldliness. This too is a part of James's God-fearing view of practical Christian perfection. To visit orphans and widows is to act according to God's loving heart, a characteristic of perfection on the positive side, and to keep oneself unspotted from the world is to be separated from the world according to God's holy nature, a characteristic of perfection on the negative side.

refs.text_gb: 学习行善；寻求公平，解救受欺压的；给孤儿伸冤，为寡妇辨屈。
refs.text_big5: 學習行善；尋求公平，解救受欺壓的；給孤兒伸冤，為寡婦辨屈。
refs.text_en: Learn to do good. / Seek justice; / Correct the ruthless. / Defend the orphan; / Plead for the widow.

verses.text_gb: 我的[Cra]弟兄们，你们既[Fn1][Crb]相信[Fn2]我们[Crc]荣耀的主耶稣基督，便不可[Crd]按着外貌待人。
verses.text_big5: 我的[Cra]弟兄們，你們既[Fn1][Crb]相信[Fn2]我們[Crc]榮耀的主耶穌基督，便不可[Crd]按著外貌待人。
verses.text_en: My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ of glory with respect of persons.
verses.text_gb_plain: 我的弟兄们，你们既相信我们荣耀的主耶稣基督，便不可按着外貌待人。
verses.text_big5_plain: 我的弟兄們，你們既相信我們榮耀的主耶穌基督，便不可按著外貌待人。

footnotes.zh: 直译，有我们荣耀的主耶稣基督的信，或，有在我们荣耀的主耶稣基督里的信。参罗三22注1。这指明本书信，特别本章，是写给在荣耀的主耶稣基督里新约的信徒。
footnotes.zh_big5: 直譯，有我們榮耀的主耶穌基督的信，或，有在我們榮耀的主耶穌基督裏的信。參羅三22註1。這指明本書信，特別本章，是寫給在榮耀的主耶穌基督裏新約的信徒。
footnotes.en: 2:1 1 faith Or, faith in our Lord...; cf. note Rom. 3:22 1 . This indicates that this Epistle, and especially this chapter, was written to the New Testament believers in the Lord Jesus Christ of glory.

footnotes.zh: 译者多半译为，我们的主耶稣基督，荣耀的主。
footnotes.zh_big5: 譯者多半譯為，我們的主耶穌基督，榮耀的主。
footnotes.en: 2:1 2 of Most translators add, the Lord.

refs.text_gb: 我亲爱的弟兄们，请听，神岂不是拣选了世上贫穷的人，叫他们在信上富足，并承受祂所应许给那些爱祂之人的国么？
refs.text_big5: 我親愛的弟兄們，請聽，神豈不是揀選了世上貧窮的人，叫他們在信上富足，並承受祂所應許給那些愛祂之人的國麼？
refs.text_en: Listen, my beloved brothers: Did not God choose the poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom, which He promised to those who love Him?

refs.text_gb: 我的弟兄们，若有人说自己有信心，却没有行为，有什么益处？难道这信心能救他么？
refs.text_big5: 我的弟兄們，若有人說自己有信心，卻沒有行為，有甚麼益處？難道這信心能救他麼？
refs.text_en: What is the profit, my brothers, if anyone says he has faith but does not have works? Can that faith save him?

refs.text_gb: 我的弟兄们，无论何时你们落在诸般的试炼中，都要以为大喜乐；
refs.text_big5: 我的弟兄們，無論何時你們落在諸般的試煉中，都要以為大喜樂；
refs.text_en: Count it all joy, my brothers, whenever you fall into various trials,

refs.text_gb: 就是神的义，借着信耶稣基督，归与一切信的人，并没有分别。
refs.text_big5: 就是神的義，藉著信耶穌基督，歸與一切信的人，並沒有分別。
refs.text_en: Even the righteousness of God through the faith of Jesus Christ to all those who believe, for there is no distinction;

refs.text_gb: 我们是生来的犹太人，并不是出于外邦的罪人，
refs.text_big5: 我們是生來的猶太人，並不是出於外邦的罪人，
refs.text_en: We are Jews by nature and not sinners from among the Gentiles;

refs.text_gb: 且知道人得称义，不是本于行律法，乃是借着信耶稣基督，连我们也信入了基督耶稣，使我们本于信基督得称义，不是本于行律法；因为凡属肉体的人，都不能本于行律法得称义。
refs.text_big5: 且知道人得稱義，不是本於行律法，乃是藉著信耶穌基督，連我們也信入了基督耶穌，使我們本於信基督得稱義，不是本於行律法；因為凡屬肉體的人，都不能本於行律法得稱義。
refs.text_en: And knowing that a man is not justified out of works of law, but through faith in Jesus Christ, we also have believed into Christ Jesus that we might be justified out of faith in Christ and not out of the works of law, because out of the works of law no flesh will be justified.

refs.text_gb: 但圣经把众人都圈在罪里，好叫那以信耶稣基督为本的应许，可以赐给那些信的人。
refs.text_big5: 但聖經把眾人都圈在罪裏，好叫那以信耶穌基督為本的應許，可以賜給那些信的人。
refs.text_en: But the Scripture has shut up all under sin in order that the promise out of faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.

refs.text_gb: 因为你们众人借着相信基督耶稣，都是神的儿子。
refs.text_big5: 因為你們眾人藉著相信基督耶穌，都是神的兒子。
refs.text_en: For you are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.

refs.text_gb: 这智慧，这世代有权有位的人，并没有一个知道，因为他们若知道，就不会把荣耀的主钉十字架了。
refs.text_big5: 這智慧，這世代有權有位的人，並沒有一個知道，因為他們若知道，就不會把榮耀的主釘十字架了。
refs.text_en: Which none of the rulers of this age have known; for if they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory;

refs.text_gb: 但你们若按外貌待人，便是犯罪，给律法定为犯法的。
refs.text_big5: 但你們若按外貌待人，便是犯罪，給律法定為犯法的。
refs.text_en: But if you respect persons, you commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.

refs.text_gb: 审判的时候，不可看人的外貌；听讼不可分尊卑，不可怕人的脸面，因为审判是属于神的。若有难断的案件，可以呈到我这里来，我就听审。
refs.text_big5: 審判的時候，不可看人的外貌；聽訟不可分尊卑，不可怕人的臉面，因為審判是屬於神的。若有難斷的案件，可以呈到我這裏來，我就聽審。
refs.text_en: You shall not respect persons in judgment; you shall hear the small and the great alike. You shall not fear the face of man, for judgment is God's. And the case that is too hard for you, you shall bring to me; and I will hear it.

refs.text_gb: 不可屈枉公理，不可看人的外貌，也不可受贿赂，因为贿赂能叫智慧人的眼变瞎，又能颠倒义人的话。
refs.text_big5: 不可屈枉公理，不可看人的外貌，也不可受賄賂，因為賄賂能叫智慧人的眼變瞎，又能顛倒義人的話。
refs.text_en: You shall not distort justice; you shall not respect persons, nor shall you take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and perverts the words of the righteous.

refs.text_gb: 于是打发他们的门徒，同希律党的人到耶稣那里，说，夫子，我们知道你是诚实的，并且诚诚实实教导神的道路，什么人你都不顾忌，因为你不看人的外貌。
refs.text_big5: 於是打發他們的門徒，同希律黨的人到耶穌那裏，說，夫子，我們知道你是誠實的，並且誠誠實實教導神的道路，甚麼人你都不顧忌，因為你不看人的外貌。
refs.text_en: And they sent to Him their disciples with the Herodians, saying, Teacher, we know that You are true and that You teach the way of God in truth and do not fear anyone, for You do not regard the person of men.

refs.text_gb: 因为神并不偏待人。
refs.text_big5: 因為神並不偏待人。
refs.text_en: For there is no respect of persons with God.

refs.text_gb: 祂不徇掌权者的情面，也不看重富足的过于贫穷的；因为他们都是祂手所造的。
refs.text_big5: 祂不徇掌權者的情面，也不看重富足的過於貧窮的；因為他們都是祂手所造的。
refs.text_en: He who does not respect the persons of princes, / Nor regard the rich man more than the poor, / For they are all the work of His hands?

verses.text_big5: 若有一個人戴著[Cra]金戒指，穿著華麗衣服，進你們的[Fn1]會堂去，又有一個[Crb]窮人，穿著骯髒衣服也進去；
verses.text_en: For if there comes into your synagogue a man with gold rings in splendid clothing, and there also comes in a poor man in filthy clothing,
verses.text_gb_plain: 若有一个人戴着金戒指，穿着华丽衣服，进你们的会堂去，又有一个穷人，穿着肮脏衣服也进去；
verses.text_big5_plain: 若有一個人戴著金戒指，穿著華麗衣服，進你們的會堂去，又有一個窮人，穿著骯髒衣服也進去；

footnotes.zh: 原文是由“一起”和“带来”组成的。因此是集合、聚集、会众；转意为聚集的地方。本辞在新约用以指犹太人的聚集(徒十三43，九2，路十二11)和聚集的地方(路七5)，在那里他们研读圣经，寻求关乎神的知识(路四16～17，徒十三14～15)。在耶路撒冷，有好些各类犹太人的会堂(徒六9)。雅各在这里用会堂这辞，也许指明犹太信徒认为他们的聚集和聚集的地方，也是犹太会堂中的一个。若是如此，这就和整本书信一样，带有犹太特征；并且可能指明犹太基督徒认为，他们仍是犹太人的一部分，是按着旧约作神选民的；他们对于旧约神的选民与新约在基督里信徒的分别，缺少清楚的异象。见一1注4。
footnotes.zh_big5: 原文是由“一起”和“帶來”組成的。因此是集合、聚集、會眾；轉意為聚集的地方。本辭在新約用以指猶太人的聚集（徒十三43，九2，路十二11）和聚集的地方，（路七5，）在那裏他們研讀聖經，尋求關乎神的知識。（路四16～17，徒十三14～15。）在耶路撒冷，有好些各類猶太人的會堂。（徒六9。）雅各在這裏用會堂這辭，也許指明猶太信徒認為他們的聚集和聚集的地方，也是猶太會堂中的一個。若是如此，這就和整本書信一樣，帶有猶太特徵；並且可能指明猶太基督徒認為，他們仍是猶太人的一部分，是按著舊約作神選民的；他們對於舊約神的選民與新約在基督裏信徒的分別，缺少清楚的異象。見一1註4。
footnotes.en: 2:2 1 synagogue The Greek word is composed of together and to bring; hence, a collecting, gathering, congregating; and thence, the place of gathering. It was used in the New Testament to denote the congregation of the Jews (Acts 13:43; 9:2; Luke 12:11) and their congregating place (Luke 7:5), where they sought the knowledge of God by studying the Holy Scriptures (Luke 4:16-17; Acts 13:14-15). In Jerusalem there were numerous synagogues for different groups of Jews (Acts 6:9). James's use of this word here may indicate that the Jewish believers considered their assembly and assembling place as another of the synagogues among the Jews. If so, this bears, as does the whole Epistle, a Jewish character and may indicate that the Jewish Christians regarded themselves as still a part of the Jewish people, the chosen people of God according to the Old Testament, and that they lacked a clear vision concerning the distinction between God's chosen people of the Old Testament and the believers in Christ of the New Testament. See note James 1:1 3 .

refs.text_gb: 照样，也愿女人穿着正派合宜，以廉耻、自守，不以编发、黄金、珍珠、或贵价的衣服，妆饰自己，
refs.text_big5: 照樣，也願女人穿著正派合宜，以廉恥、自守，不以編髮、黃金、珍珠、或貴價的衣服，妝飾自己，
refs.text_en: Similarly, that women adorn themselves in proper clothing with modesty and sobriety, not with braided hair and gold or pearls or costly clothing,

refs.text_gb: 你们的妆饰，不要重于外面的辫头发、戴金饰、穿衣服，
refs.text_big5: 你們的妝飾，不要重於外面的辮頭髮、戴金飾、穿衣服，
refs.text_en: Let your adorning not be the outward plaiting of hair and putting on of gold or clothing with garments,

refs.text_gb: 只是要我们记念穷人，这也是我本来热诚去行的。
refs.text_big5: 只是要我們記念窮人，這也是我本來熱誠去行的。
refs.text_en: Only they requested that we remember the poor, which very thing I was also eager to do.

refs.text_gb: 贫穷人说哀求的话；富足人厉声以对。
refs.text_big5: 貧窮人說哀求的話；富足人厲聲以對。
refs.text_en: The poor man utters supplications, / But the rich man answers roughly.

refs.text_gb: 怜悯穷人的，就是借给耶和华；他的善行，耶和华必偿还。
refs.text_big5: 憐憫窮人的，就是借給耶和華；他的善行，耶和華必償還。
refs.text_en: He who has pity upon a poor man lends to Jehovah, / And He will repay him for his good deed.

refs.text_gb: 眼目慈善的，就必蒙福，因他将食物分给穷人。
refs.text_big5: 眼目慈善的，就必蒙福，因他將食物分給窮人。
refs.text_en: He who is generous will be blessed, / For he gives some of his bread to the poor.

verses.text_gb: 你们就重看那穿华丽衣服的人，说，请你坐在这好位上；又对那穷人说，你站在那里，或坐在我脚凳下边。
verses.text_big5: 你們就重看那穿華麗衣服的人，說，請你坐在這好位上；又對那窮人說，你站在那裏，或坐在我腳凳下邊。
verses.text_en: And you look upon the one wearing the splendid clothing and say, You sit here in a good place, and to the poor man you say, You stand there, or sit under my footstool;
verses.text_gb_plain: 你们就重看那穿华丽衣服的人，说，请你坐在这好位上；又对那穷人说，你站在那里，或坐在我脚凳下边。
verses.text_big5_plain: 你們就重看那穿華麗衣服的人，說，請你坐在這好位上；又對那窮人說，你站在那裏，或坐在我腳凳下邊。

verses.text_gb: 这岂不是[Fn1]你们中间有了[Cra]歧视，用恶意判断人么？
verses.text_big5: 這豈不是[Fn1]你們中間有了[Cra]歧視，用惡意判斷人麼？
verses.text_en: Have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil reasonings?
verses.text_gb_plain: 这岂不是你们中间有了歧视，用恶意判断人么？
verses.text_big5_plain: 這豈不是你們中間有了歧視，用惡意判斷人麼？

footnotes.zh: 或，你们里面。在基督徒的弟兄们中间，存在着富人和穷人的区别，因而有了歧视，这对于主和祂神圣生命的救恩，乃是羞耻。
footnotes.zh_big5: 或，你們裏面。在基督徒的弟兄們中間，存在著富人和窮人的區別，因而有了歧視，這對於主和祂神聖生命的救恩，乃是羞恥。
footnotes.en: 2:4 1 distinctions The distinctions that existed between the rich and the poor among the Christian brothers and that resulted in discrimination were a shame to the Lord and to the salvation of His divine life.

refs.text_gb: 唯独从上头来的智慧，先是纯洁的，后是和平的、和蔼的、柔顺的，满有怜悯和善果，没有偏见，没有假冒。
refs.text_big5: 惟獨從上頭來的智慧，先是純潔的，後是和平的、和藹的、柔順的，滿有憐憫和善果，沒有偏見，沒有假冒。
refs.text_en: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, forbearing, compliant, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, without hypocrisy.

footnotes.zh: 8～11节的话指明，在雅各的时候，犹太信徒仍然遵守旧约的律法。这符合雅各和耶路撒冷的众长老，在徒二一20对保罗所说的话。雅各和耶路撒冷的众长老，以及成万的犹太信徒，仍留在基督徒信仰与摩西律法的混杂里。他们甚至劝保罗实行这种半犹太教的混杂作法(徒二一17～26)。他们不知道律法时代已经完全过去，恩典时代该受完全的尊重；凡不顾这两个时代之分别的，就是抵挡神时代的行政，就是严重破坏神建造召会作基督彰显的经纶计划。这样看来，本书是在半犹太教混杂的乌云，模糊不清的背景下写的。然而有好些按天然观念实行虔敬的人，却忽视了本书的这种背景。
footnotes.zh_big5: 8～11節的話指明，在雅各的時候，猶太信徒仍然遵守舊約的律法。這符合雅各和耶路撒冷的眾長老，在徒二一20對保羅所說的話。雅各和耶路撒冷的眾長老，以及成萬的猶太信徒，仍留在基督徒信仰與摩西律法的混雜裏。他們甚至勸保羅實行這種半猶太教的混雜作法。（徒二一17～26。）他們不知道律法時代已經完全過去，恩典時代該受完全的尊重；凡不顧這兩個時代之分別的，就是抵擋神時代的行政，就是嚴重破壞神建造召會作基督彰顯的經綸計畫。這樣看來，本書是在半猶太教混雜的烏雲，糢糊不清的背景下寫的。然而有好些按天然觀念實行虔敬的人，卻忽視了本書的這種背景。
footnotes.en: 2:10 1 keeps The word in vv. 8-11 indicates that the Jewish believers at James's time were still practicing the keeping of the Old Testament law. This corresponds with the word in Acts 21:20 spoken to Paul by James and the elders in Jerusalem. James, the elders in Jerusalem, and many thousands of Jewish believers were still in a mixture of the Christian faith and the Mosaic law. They even advised Paul to practice such a semi-Judaic mixture (Acts 21:17-26). They were unaware that the dispensation of law was altogether over and that the dispensation of grace should be fully honored, and that any disregard of the distinction between these two dispensations would be against God's dispensational administration and would be a great damage to God's economical plan for the building up of the church as the expression of Christ. Thus, this Epistle was written under the cloud of a semi-Judaic mixture, under a background that was obscured. Many who practice religion according to their natural concept neglect the background seen in this book.
